        """One immutable policy snapshot per service/deployment."""
        
        import hashlib
        import json
        from pathlib import Path
        
        from pydantic import TypeAdapter
        
        from app.identity.aliases import Aliases
        from app.schemas.ingest import SourceConfig
        from app.schemas.normalized import ApplicationAttributes, DeviceAttributes, UserAttributes
        
        ATTRIBUTES = {"device": DeviceAttributes, "user": UserAttributes, "application": ApplicationAttributes}
        PIPELINE_VERSION = "phase3-v1"
        
        
        def load_sources(path: str | Path) -> list[SourceConfig]:
            data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if not isinstance(data, list):
                raise ValueError("Source configuration must be an array")
            # Accept the existing sample manifest as well as a plain list of source definitions.
            return TypeAdapter(list[SourceConfig]).validate_python([
                entry["source"] if isinstance(entry, dict) and "source" in entry else entry for entry in data
            ])
        
        
        class Policy:
            def __init__(self, sources: list[SourceConfig]):
                self.sources = [s.model_copy(deep=True) for s in sources]
                if len({(s.organization_id, s.source_id) for s in sources}) != len(sources):
                    raise ValueError("Duplicate source configuration")
                self.aliases = Aliases(self.sources)
                self.authorities: dict[tuple[str, str, str], str] = {}
                for source in self.sources:
                    for attribute in source.authoritative_attributes:
                        kind, separator, field = attribute.partition(".")
                        if not separator or kind not in ATTRIBUTES or (
                            field not in ATTRIBUTES[kind].model_fields and (kind, field) != ("device", "assigned_to")
                        ) or field == "groups":
                            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported authoritative attribute: {attribute}")
                        key = source.organization_id, kind, field
                        if key in self.authorities and self.authorities[key] != source.source_id:
                            raise ValueError("Only one source can be authoritative for an attribute")
                        self.authorities[key] = source.source_id
                content = [s.model_dump(mode="json") for s in sorted(self.sources, key=lambda s: (s.organization_id, s.source_id))]
                self.version = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(
                    {"pipeline": PIPELINE_VERSION, "sources": content}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
                ).encode()).hexdigest()
        
            def authority(self, organization: str, kind: str, field: str) -> str | None:
                return self.authorities.get((organization, kind, field))
        EOF
        cat > app/reconciliation/projection.py <<'EOF'
        """Rebuild an affected CI's scalar projection from retained observations."""
        
        from sqlalchemy import select
        
        from app.db.models import Observation, User, UserGroup
        from app.reconciliation.evidence import Candidate, choose
        from app.reconciliation.policy import ATTRIBUTES, Policy
        
        
        def project_attributes(session, ci, observations: list[Observation], policy: Policy):
            state = dict(ci.field_state or {})
            entity_observations = [o for o in observations if o.normalized_record.get("record_kind") == "entity"]
            for field in ATTRIBUTES[ci.kind].model_fields:
                if field == "groups":
                    continue
                candidates = [Candidate(o.normalized_record.get("attributes", {}).get(field), o.id,
                                        o.run.source_id, o.observed_at,
                                        o.normalized_record.get("reference_only", False)) for o in entity_observations]
                selected = choose(candidates, policy.authority(ci.organization_id, ci.kind, field))
                if selected is not None:
                    setattr(ci, field, selected.value)
                    state[field] = {"status": selected.status, "observation_ids": list(selected.observation_ids)}
            if isinstance(ci, User):
                groups = {group for o in entity_observations
                          for group in o.normalized_record.get("attributes", {}).get("groups", [])}
                current = set(session.scalars(select(UserGroup.group_name).where(UserGroup.user_id == ci.id)))
                for group in sorted(groups - current):
                    session.add(UserGroup(user_id=ci.id, group_name=group))
            ci.is_reference = not any(not o.normalized_record.get("reference_only", False) for o in entity_observations)
            primary = {"device": "hostname", "user": "name", "application": "name"}[ci.kind]
            ci.display_name = getattr(ci, primary) or f"{ci.kind}:{ci.id}"
            ci.field_state = state
        EOF

        from dataclasses import dataclass
        
        from app.identity.resolver import IdentityInput, Resolution
        from app.schemas.normalized import NormalizedRecord, RelationshipAssertion
        
        
        @dataclass
        class ResolvedAssertion:
            record_index: int
            assertion_index: int
            record: NormalizedRecord
            assertion: RelationshipAssertion
            source_ci_id: str
            resolution: Resolution
        
        
        def resolve_targets(resolver, records, roots) -> list[ResolvedAssertion]:
            items = []
            pending = []
            for i, record in enumerate(records):
                root = roots[f"r:{i}"]
                if root.ci is None:
                    continue
                for j, assertion in enumerate(record.relationships):
                    token = f"e:{i}:{j}"
                    target = assertion.target
                    items.append(IdentityInput(token, target.ci_type, record.organization_id,
                                               target.identifiers, reference_only=True))
                    pending.append((token, i, j, record, assertion, root.ci.id))
            outcomes = resolver.resolve_many(items)
            result = []
            for token, i, j, record, assertion, source_id in pending:
                outcome = outcomes[token]
                # Self edges remain evidence but never enter the constrained current graph.
                if outcome.ci is not None and outcome.ci.id == source_id:
                    outcome = Resolution("unresolved", candidate_ids=(source_id,))
                result.append(ResolvedAssertion(i, j, record, assertion, source_id, outcome))
            return result
        EOF

        """Project current typed edges; assignment is scalar, other assertions additive."""
        
        from sqlalchemy import select
        
        from app.db.models import Relationship
        from app.reconciliation.evidence import Candidate, choose
        
        
        def project_relationships(session, ci, observations, policy):
            current = list(session.scalars(select(Relationship).where(Relationship.from_ci_id == ci.id)))
            assertions = [o for o in observations
                          if o.normalized_record.get("record_kind") == "relationship"
                          and o.resolution_status == "resolved"
                          and o.normalized_record.get("target_ci_id") is not None]
            assignment = [Candidate(o.normalized_record["target_ci_id"], o.id, o.run.source_id, o.observed_at)
                          for o in assertions if o.normalized_record["relation_type"] == "assigned_to"]
            selected = choose(assignment, policy.authority(ci.organization_id, ci.kind, "assigned_to"))
            if selected is not None:
                state = dict(ci.field_state or {})
                state["assigned_to"] = {"status": selected.status, "observation_ids": list(selected.observation_ids)}
                ci.field_state = state
                removed = [edge for edge in current if edge.relation_type == "assigned_to" and edge.to_ci_id != selected.value]
                for edge in removed:
                    session.delete(edge)
                if removed:
                    # Release the partial unique assignment key before inserting its replacement.
                    session.flush()
                current = [edge for edge in current if edge not in removed]
            wanted = {(o.normalized_record["relation_type"], o.normalized_record["target_ci_id"])
                      for o in assertions if o.normalized_record["relation_type"] != "assigned_to"}
            if selected is not None and selected.value is not None:
                wanted.add(("assigned_to", selected.value))
            existing = {(edge.relation_type, edge.to_ci_id) for edge in current}
            for relation, target in sorted(wanted - existing):
                session.add(Relationship(from_ci_id=ci.id, to_ci_id=target, relation_type=relation))

        """Atomic CMDB ingestion and exact-replay handling over prepared records."""
        
        from collections import defaultdict
        import hashlib
        
        from sqlalchemy import select
        from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError, OperationalError
        from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload
        
        from app.db.models import IngestionRun, Observation, Relationship, new_id, utc_now
        from app.identity.resolver import IdentityInput, IdentityResolver, fingerprint
        from app.ingestion.errors import InputError
        from app.ingestion.relationships import resolve_targets
        from app.ingestion.service import prepare_ingestion
        from app.reconciliation.policy import Policy
        from app.reconciliation.projection import project_attributes
        from app.reconciliation.relationships import project_relationships
        
        
        class DatabaseBusy(RuntimeError):
            pass
        
        
        class WarningLog:
            def __init__(self, prepared):
                self.count = prepared.warning_count
                self.items = [w.model_dump(mode="json") for w in prepared.warnings]
        
            def add(self, code, path, message, **details):
                self.count += 1
                if len(self.items) < 50:
                    self.items.append(dict(code=code, path=path, message=message, **details))
        
        
        def _observations(session, ids):
            grouped = defaultdict(list)
            ids = sorted(ids)
            for start in range(0, len(ids), 400):
                rows = session.scalars(select(Observation).options(selectinload(Observation.run)).where(
                    Observation.ci_id.in_(ids[start:start + 400])
                ))
                for row in rows:
                    grouped[row.ci_id].append(row)
            return grouped
        
        
        def _edges(session, ids):
            keys = set()
            ids = sorted(ids)
            for start in range(0, len(ids), 400):
                keys.update(session.execute(select(Relationship.from_ci_id, Relationship.relation_type,
                                                   Relationship.to_ci_id).where(
                    Relationship.from_ci_id.in_(ids[start:start + 400])
                )).all())
            return keys
        
        
        class IngestService:
            def __init__(self, sessions, policy: Policy, *, adapters=None):
                self.sessions = sessions
                self.policy = policy
                self.adapters = adapters
        
            def ingest(self, request):
                prepared = prepare_ingestion(request, self.policy.sources, adapters=self.adapters)
                return self.persist(request, prepared)
        
            def persist(self, request, prepared):
                """Persist validated preparation. Future AI extraction can use this boundary too."""
                if (request.organization_id, request.source_id) != (prepared.organization_id, prepared.source_id) or any(
                    row.organization_id != request.organization_id for row in prepared.batch.records
                ):
                    raise InputError("Prepared batch does not match the requested source/organization")
                replay_key = dict(organization_id=request.organization_id, source_id=request.source_id,
                                  payload_sha256=hashlib.sha256(request.content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
                                  policy_version=self.policy.version)
                try:
                    with self.sessions.begin() as session:
                        # Serialize SQLite writers before identity reads, avoiding stale read-to-write upgrades.
                        session.connection(execution_options={"sqlite_write": True})
                        previous = session.scalar(select(IngestionRun).filter_by(**replay_key))
                        if previous is not None:
                            return previous.result | {"replayed": True}
                        return self._write(session, request, prepared, replay_key)
                except (IntegrityError, OperationalError) as exc:
                    # A racing exact replay may have committed while this transaction lost a race.
                    try:
                        with self.sessions() as session:
                            previous = session.scalar(select(IngestionRun).filter_by(**replay_key))
                            if previous is not None:
                                return previous.result | {"replayed": True}
                    except OperationalError:
                        pass
                    if isinstance(exc, OperationalError) and any(word in str(exc).lower() for word in ("locked", "busy")):
                        raise DatabaseBusy("Database is busy; retry the request") from exc
                    raise
        
            def _write(self, session, request, prepared, replay_key):
                log = WarningLog(prepared)
                now = utc_now()
                run = IngestionRun(id=new_id(), **replay_key, format=request.format,
                                   received_at=now, completed_at=now, result={})
                session.add(run)
                resolver = IdentityResolver(session, self.policy.aliases)
                records = prepared.batch.records
                roots = resolver.resolve_many([
                    IdentityInput(f"r:{i}", row.ci_type, row.organization_id, row.identifiers)
                    for i, row in enumerate(records)
                ])
                quarantined = 0
                for i, record in enumerate(records):
                    resolved = roots[f"r:{i}"]
                    if resolved.ci is None:
                        quarantined += 1
                        log.add("identity_conflict" if resolved.status == "identity_conflict" else "missing_identifiers",
                                record.record_key, "Record retained without changing any CI",
                                candidate_ids=list(resolved.candidate_ids))
                    data = record.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"raw_record"}, exclude_unset=True)
                    data.update(record_kind="entity", reference_only=False, candidate_ids=list(resolved.candidate_ids),
                                attributes=record.attributes.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_unset=True, exclude_none=True),
                                source_metadata=prepared.source_metadata)
                    session.add(Observation(id=new_id(), run=run, ci=resolved.ci, record_key=record.record_key,
                                            observed_at=record.observed_at, raw_record=record.raw_record,
                                            normalized_record=data, origin="adapter", resolution_status=resolved.status))
                session.flush()
                evidence = _observations(session, resolver.touched)
                for ci in list(resolver.touched.values()):
                    project_attributes(session, ci, evidence[ci.id], self.policy)
        
                # All root CIs exist before targets are resolved, so forward references are safe.
                assertions = resolve_targets(resolver, records, roots)
                session.flush()
                before_edges = _edges(session, resolver.touched)
                unresolved = 0
                for edge in assertions:
                    target = edge.resolution.ci
                    if target is None:
                        unresolved += 1
                        log.add("unresolved_reference", edge.record.record_key,
                                "Relationship target has no unambiguous stable identity",
                                candidate_ids=list(edge.resolution.candidate_ids),
                                relation_type=edge.assertion.relation_type)
                    token = f"{edge.record.record_key}/_cmdb/relationships/{edge.assertion_index}"
                    data = dict(record_kind="relationship", relation_type=edge.assertion.relation_type,
                                target=edge.assertion.target.model_dump(mode="json"),
                                target_ci_id=target.id if target else None,
                                candidate_ids=list(edge.resolution.candidate_ids),
                                evidence=edge.assertion.evidence.model_dump(mode="json") if edge.assertion.evidence else None)
                    session.add(Observation(id=new_id(), run=run, ci_id=edge.source_ci_id,
                                            record_key=token, observed_at=edge.record.observed_at,
                                            raw_record={"reference": edge.assertion.target.display_name},
                                            normalized_record=data, origin="adapter", resolution_status=edge.resolution.status))
                    if target is not None:
                        canonical = [self.policy.aliases.canonical(i) for i in edge.assertion.target.identifiers]
                        name = next((i.value for i in canonical if i.scope.identifier_type == "app_name"), None)
                        attributes = {"name": name} if target.kind == "application" and name else {}
                        session.add(Observation(id=new_id(), run=run, ci=target,
                                                record_key=f"{edge.record.record_key}/_cmdb/references/{edge.assertion_index}",
                                                observed_at=edge.record.observed_at,
                                                raw_record={"reference": edge.assertion.target.display_name},
                                                normalized_record=dict(record_kind="entity", reference_only=True, attributes=attributes,
                                                                       identifiers=[i.model_dump(mode="json") for i in canonical]),
                                                origin="adapter", resolution_status="resolved"))
                session.flush()
                evidence = _observations(session, resolver.touched)
                for ci in resolver.touched.values():
                    project_attributes(session, ci, evidence[ci.id], self.policy)
                    project_relationships(session, ci, evidence[ci.id], self.policy)
                    for field, state in ci.field_state.items():
                        if state["status"] == "conflict":
                            log.add("attribute_conflict", f"/ci/{ci.id}/{field}",
                                    "Competing evidence has no defensible winner; field is unknown",
                                    observation_ids=state["observation_ids"])
                session.flush()
                after_edges = _edges(session, resolver.touched)
                updated = sum(fingerprint(ci) != resolver.before[ci_id]
                              for ci_id, ci in resolver.touched.items() if ci_id not in resolver.created)
                result = dict(
                    run_id=run.id, replayed=False,
                    records=dict(received=len(records), resolved=len(records) - quarantined, quarantined=quarantined),
                    entities=dict(created=len(resolver.created), updated=updated,
                                  unchanged=len(resolver.touched) - len(resolver.created) - updated),
                    relationships=dict(created=len(after_edges - before_edges), removed=len(before_edges - after_edges),
                                       unchanged=len(before_edges & after_edges)),
                    warning_count=log.count, warnings=log.items, unresolved_reference_count=unresolved,
                )
                run.completed_at = utc_now()
                run.result = result
                session.flush()
                return result
        EOF

        """Read-only CI projections and bounded evidence/edge pagination."""
        
        from sqlalchemy import func, literal, select, union_all
        
        from app.db.models import ConfigurationItem, IngestionRun, Observation, Relationship
        from app.identity.resolver import MODELS
        from app.reconciliation.policy import ATTRIBUTES
        
        
        class MissingCI(LookupError):
            pass
        
        
        class InventoryService:
            def __init__(self, session, organization_id):
                self.session = session
                self.organization_id = organization_id
        
            def view(self, ci):
                values = {field: getattr(ci, field) for field in ATTRIBUTES[ci.kind].model_fields if field != "groups"}
                if ci.kind == "user":
                    values["groups"] = sorted(group.group_name for group in ci.groups)
                output = dict(id=ci.id, kind=ci.kind, display_name=ci.display_name,
                              is_reference=ci.is_reference, created_at=ci.created_at, updated_at=ci.updated_at,
                              attributes=ATTRIBUTES[ci.kind](**values).model_dump(mode="json"),
                              has_conflicts=any(s["status"] == "conflict" for s in ci.field_state.values()))
                if ci.kind == "device":
                    output["assigned_user_id"] = self.session.scalar(select(Relationship.to_ci_id).where(
                        Relationship.from_ci_id == ci.id, Relationship.relation_type == "assigned_to"))
                elif ci.kind == "application":
                    output["observed_assignment_count"] = self.session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Relationship).where(
                        Relationship.to_ci_id == ci.id, Relationship.relation_type == "uses"))
                    output["owner_user_ids"] = list(self.session.scalars(select(Relationship.to_ci_id).where(
                        Relationship.from_ci_id == ci.id, Relationship.relation_type == "owned_by").order_by(Relationship.to_ci_id)))
                return output
        
            def list(self, kind, filters, limit, offset):
                model = MODELS[kind]
                allowed = {"device": {"status", "os_family"}, "user": {"status", "mfa_enabled"}, "application": {"app_type"}}
                if not set(filters).issubset(allowed[kind]):
                    raise ValueError("Unsupported inventory filter")
                predicates = [model.organization_id == self.organization_id]
                predicates.extend(getattr(model, field) == value for field, value in filters.items() if value is not None)
                total = self.session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(model).where(*predicates))
                items = self.session.scalars(select(model).where(*predicates).order_by(model.id).limit(limit).offset(offset)).all()
                return dict(data=[self.view(ci) for ci in items], total=total, limit=limit, offset=offset)
        
            def detail(self, ci_id, edge_limit, edge_offset):
                ci = self.session.get(ConfigurationItem, ci_id)
                if ci is None or ci.organization_id != self.organization_id:
                    raise MissingCI("Configuration item not found")
                output = self.view(ci)
                graph = union_all(
                    select(Relationship.id, literal("out").label("direction"), Relationship.relation_type,
                           Relationship.to_ci_id.label("other_ci_id")).where(Relationship.from_ci_id == ci_id),
                    select(Relationship.id, literal("in").label("direction"), Relationship.relation_type,
                           Relationship.from_ci_id.label("other_ci_id")).where(Relationship.to_ci_id == ci_id),
                ).subquery()
                edges = self.session.execute(select(graph).order_by(graph.c.direction, graph.c.relation_type, graph.c.id)
                                             .limit(edge_limit).offset(edge_offset)).mappings().all()
                output.update(identifiers=[dict(id=i.id, namespace=i.namespace, value=i.value)
                                           for i in sorted(ci.identifiers, key=lambda i: (i.namespace, i.value))],
                              field_state=ci.field_state,
                              relationships=dict(data=[dict(row) for row in edges],
                                                 total=self.session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(graph)),
                                                 limit=edge_limit, offset=edge_offset))
                rows = self.session.execute(select(Observation, IngestionRun.source_id)
                                            .join(IngestionRun).where(Observation.ci_id == ci_id)
                                            .order_by(IngestionRun.completed_at.desc(), Observation.record_key, Observation.id)
                                            .limit(20)).all()
                output["provenance"] = dict(total=self.session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Observation).where(
                    Observation.ci_id == ci_id)), data=[dict(
                        observation_id=obs.id, source_id=source, run_id=obs.run_id, record_key=obs.record_key,
                        observed_at=obs.observed_at, resolution_status=obs.resolution_status,
                        origin=obs.origin, attributes=obs.normalized_record.get("attributes", {}),
                        relation_type=obs.normalized_record.get("relation_type"),
                        target_ci_id=obs.normalized_record.get("target_ci_id"),
                    ) for obs, source in rows])
                unresolved = self.session.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Observation).where(
                    Observation.ci_id == ci_id, Observation.resolution_status != "resolved",
                    Observation.normalized_record["record_kind"].as_string() == "relationship"))
                output["warnings"] = ([dict(code="unresolved_references", count=unresolved)] if unresolved else [])
                return output

        from typing import Annotated, Literal
        from uuid import UUID
        
        from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Query, Request
        
        from app.api.inventory_service import InventoryService
        
        router = APIRouter()
        Limit = Annotated[int, Query(ge=1, le=100)]
        Offset = Annotated[int, Query(ge=0, le=10000)]
        
        
        def inventory_service(request: Request):
            with request.app.state.sessions() as session:
                yield InventoryService(session, request.app.state.settings.organization_id)
        
        
        Inventory = Annotated[InventoryService, Depends(inventory_service)]
        
        
        @router.get("/devices")
        def devices(service: Inventory, status: Literal["active", "inactive", "unknown"] | None = None,
                    os_family: str | None = None, limit: Limit = 50, offset: Offset = 0):
            return service.list("device", dict(status=status, os_family=os_family), limit, offset)
        
        
        @router.get("/users")
        def users(service: Inventory, status: Literal["active", "inactive", "suspended", "unknown"] | None = None,
                  mfa_enabled: bool | None = None, limit: Limit = 50, offset: Offset = 0):
            return service.list("user", dict(status=status, mfa_enabled=mfa_enabled), limit, offset)
        
        
        @router.get("/apps")
        def apps(service: Inventory, app_type: Literal["saas", "on_prem", "unknown"] | None = None,
                 limit: Limit = 50, offset: Offset = 0):
            return service.list("application", dict(app_type=app_type), limit, offset)
        
        
        @router.get("/ci/{ci_id}")
        def detail(ci_id: UUID, service: Inventory, edge_limit: Limit = 50, edge_offset: Offset = 0):
            return service.detail(str(ci_id), edge_limit, edge_offset)

        """Consistent, sanitized errors with server-generated request correlation IDs."""
        
        import logging
        
        from fastapi.exceptions import RequestValidationError
        from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse
        from sqlalchemy.exc import OperationalError
        from starlette.exceptions import HTTPException
        
        from app.api.inventory_service import MissingCI
        from app.ingestion.errors import InputError
        from app.ingestion.persistence import DatabaseBusy
        
        logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
        
        
        def response(request, status, code, message, details=None):
            return JSONResponse(status_code=status, content={"error": dict(
                code=code, message=message, request_id=request.state.request_id, details=details or [])})
        
        
        def install_errors(app):
            @app.exception_handler(InputError)
            async def invalid_input(request, exc):
                return response(request, 413 if exc.code == "limit_exceeded" else 422, exc.code, str(exc),
                                [dict(path=exc.path)])
        
            @app.exception_handler(RequestValidationError)
            async def validation(request, exc):
                return response(request, 422, "invalid_request", "Request validation failed", [
                    dict(path="/" + "/".join(str(p) for p in error["loc"]), type=error["type"])
                    for error in exc.errors()[:50]])
        
            @app.exception_handler(MissingCI)
            async def missing(request, exc):
                return response(request, 404, "not_found", str(exc))
        
            @app.exception_handler(DatabaseBusy)
            async def busy(request, exc):
                return response(request, 503, "database_busy", str(exc))
        
            @app.exception_handler(OperationalError)
            async def database_error(request, exc):
                if any(word in str(exc).lower() for word in ("locked", "busy")):
                    return response(request, 503, "database_busy", "Database is busy; retry the request")
                logger.error("Database request failed request_id=%s", request.state.request_id)
                return response(request, 500, "internal_error", "Internal server error")
        
            @app.exception_handler(HTTPException)
            async def http_error(request, exc):
                return response(request, exc.status_code, "http_error", "Request could not be completed")
        
            @app.exception_handler(Exception)
            async def unexpected(request, exc):
                # Avoid serializing SQL parameters, payloads, or exception text into responses/logs.
                logger.error("Request failed request_id=%s category=%s", request.state.request_id, type(exc).__name__)
                return response(request, 500, "internal_error", "Internal server error")

        """FastAPI application factory with explicit source policy and database lifetime."""
        
        from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
        from uuid import uuid4
        
        from fastapi import FastAPI
        
        from app.api.errors import install_errors
        from app.api.ingest import router as ingest_router
        from app.api.inventory import router as inventory_router
        from app.config import Settings
        from app.db.session import create_sqlite_engine, initialize_database, session_factory
        from app.ingestion.persistence import IngestService
        from app.reconciliation.policy import Policy, load_sources
        
        
        def create_app(*, settings=None, sources=None, engine=None):
            settings = settings or Settings.from_env()
            sources = load_sources(settings.source_config_path) if sources is None else sources
            if any(source.organization_id != settings.organization_id for source in sources):
                raise ValueError("All sources must belong to the configured organization")
            policy = Policy(sources)
            owns_engine = engine is None
            engine = engine or create_sqlite_engine(settings)
        
            @asynccontextmanager
            async def lifespan(app):
                initialize_database(engine)
                try:
                    yield
                finally:
                    if owns_engine:
                        engine.dispose()
        
            app = FastAPI(title="AI-first CMDB", version="0.3.0", lifespan=lifespan)
            app.state.settings = settings
            app.state.sessions = session_factory(engine)
            app.state.ingestion = IngestService(app.state.sessions, policy)
        
            @app.middleware("http")
            async def correlation_id(request, call_next):
                request.state.request_id = str(uuid4())
                response = await call_next(request)
                response.headers["X-Request-ID"] = request.state.request_id
                return response
        
            install_errors(app)
            app.include_router(ingest_router)
            app.include_router(inventory_router)
            return app
        
        
        app = create_app()
        EOF

        """Response contracts for the deterministic CMDB API."""
        
        from typing import Generic, Literal, TypeVar
        
        from pydantic import AwareDatetime, Field, JsonValue
        
        from app.schemas.normalized import Contract, Kind
        
        
        class RecordCounts(Contract):
            received: int
            resolved: int
            quarantined: int
        
        
        class EntityCounts(Contract):
            created: int
            updated: int
            unchanged: int
        
        
        class RelationshipCounts(Contract):
            created: int
            removed: int
            unchanged: int
        
        
        class IngestResponse(Contract):
            run_id: str
            replayed: bool
            records: RecordCounts
            entities: EntityCounts
            relationships: RelationshipCounts
            warning_count: int
            warnings: list[dict[str, JsonValue]]
            unresolved_reference_count: int
        
        
        class CIView(Contract):
            id: str
            kind: Kind
            display_name: str
            is_reference: bool
            created_at: AwareDatetime
            updated_at: AwareDatetime
            attributes: dict[str, JsonValue]
            has_conflicts: bool
            assigned_user_id: str | None = None
            observed_assignment_count: int | None = None
            owner_user_ids: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
        
        
        T = TypeVar("T")
        
        
        class Page(Contract, Generic[T]):
            data: list[T]
            total: int
            limit: int
            offset: int
        
        
        class EdgeView(Contract):
            id: str
            direction: Literal["in", "out"]
            relation_type: str
            other_ci_id: str
        
        
        class ObservationSummary(Contract):
            observation_id: str
            source_id: str
            run_id: str
            record_key: str
            observed_at: AwareDatetime | None
            resolution_status: str
            origin: str
            attributes: dict[str, JsonValue]
            relation_type: str | None
            target_ci_id: str | None
        
        
        class ProvenanceSummary(Contract):
            total: int
            data: list[ObservationSummary]
        
        
        class CIDetail(CIView):
            identifiers: list[dict[str, str]]
            field_state: dict[str, JsonValue]
            relationships: Page[EdgeView]
            provenance: ProvenanceSummary
            warnings: list[dict[str, JsonValue]]

        def test_reliable_snapshot_time_restores_typed_activity_attributes(engine):
            sessions = session_factory(engine)
            cfg = source("apps", adapter="applications_json", snapshot_time_path=["inventory_metadata", "export_date"])
            # Catalog counts are attributes; only the explicitly configured export time orders observations.

                                        "applications": [{"app_id": "A", "users_count": count}]}, "apps"))
            with sessions() as db:
                assert db.scalar(select(Application.reported_user_count)) == 20
        
        
        def test_assignment_replacement_conflict_and_additive_access(engine):
            from app.schemas.ingest import PreparedIngestion
            from app.schemas.normalized import NormalizedBatch
            sessions = session_factory(engine)
            cfg = source()
            service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([cfg]))
            def prepared(target, observed):
                scope = dict(organization_id="org-a", ci_type="device", authority_id="inventory", identifier_type="device_id")
                user_scope = scope | {"ci_type": "user", "identifier_type": "user_id"}
                return PreparedIngestion(organization_id="org-a", source_id="inventory", warning_count=0, warnings=[],
                    batch=NormalizedBatch.model_validate_json(json.dumps({"records": [{
                        "ci_type": "device", "organization_id": "org-a", "record_key": "/0", "attributes": {},
                        "observed_at": observed, "identifiers": [{"scope": scope, "value": "D"}],
                        "relationships": [{"relation_type": "assigned_to", "target": {
                            "ci_type": "user", "identifiers": [{"scope": user_scope, "value": target}]}}]
                    }]})))
            service.persist(request("first"), prepared("U1", "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"))
            result = service.persist(request("second"), prepared("U2", "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z"))
            assert result["relationships"]["removed"] == 1
            assert result["relationships"]["created"] == 1
            # An undated contradictory assertion makes the current assignment unknown.
            result = service.persist(request("third"), prepared("U1", None))
            assert result["relationships"]["removed"] == 1
            with sessions() as db:
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Relationship)) == 0
                device = db.scalar(select(Device))
                assert device.field_state["assigned_to"]["status"] == "conflict"
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Observation).where(
                    Observation.normalized_record["record_kind"].as_string() == "relationship")) == 3

        def test_concurrent_exact_replay_has_one_committed_run(tmp_path):
            from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
            from app.config import Settings
            from app.db.session import create_sqlite_engine, initialize_database
            engine = create_sqlite_engine(Settings(database_url=f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'concurrent.db'}"))
            initialize_database(engine)
            sessions = session_factory(engine)
            service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([source()]))
            req = request([{"device_id": "D"}])
            try:
                with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
                    results = list(pool.map(lambda _: service.ingest(req), range(2)))
                assert {r["replayed"] for r in results} == {False, True}
                assert len({r["run_id"] for r in results}) == 1
                with sessions() as db:
                    assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(IngestionRun)) == 1
                    assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Device)) == 1
            finally:
                engine.dispose()
        
        
        def test_database_lock_is_a_retryable_error(tmp_path):
            from app.config import Settings
            from app.db.session import create_sqlite_engine, initialize_database
            from app.ingestion.persistence import DatabaseBusy
            engine = create_sqlite_engine(Settings(database_url=f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'locked.db'}", sqlite_busy_timeout_ms=1))
            initialize_database(engine)
            sessions = session_factory(engine)
            try:
                with engine.connect().execution_options(sqlite_write=True) as connection:
                    transaction = connection.begin()
                    with pytest.raises(DatabaseBusy):
                        IngestService(sessions, Policy([source()])).ingest(request([{"device_id": "D"}]))
                    transaction.rollback()
                with sessions() as db:
                    assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(IngestionRun)) == 0
            finally:
                engine.dispose()

    # AI-first CMDB
    
    A proposed Python backend for combining infrastructure and SaaS inventories into a queryable Configuration Management Database (CMDB).
    
    **Status: Phase 1 foundations and Phase 2 deterministic preparation written.** SQLAlchemy models, a SQLite initializer, normalized contracts, five source adapters, and tests are present. Preparation and schema tests pass; database verification remains blocked by the unavailable SQLAlchemy dependency. API routes, persisted ingestion, entity resolution, and AI are not implemented. The complete application behavior below remains planned. See the [technical design](docs/design.md) for the schema, API contracts, resolution policies, sample-data analysis, and implementation roadmap, and the [assignment specification](STLabs_Backend_TakeHome_CMDB_Junior.md) for requirements.
    
    ## Application overview
    
    A configuration item (CI) is an entity an organization needs to track: in this prototype, a device, user, or application. Attributes describe an item, such as a device's operating system or a user's MFA status. Relationships connect items, such as a device assigned to a user or an application depending on another application.
    
    The service will ingest inventories, normalize their records, identify existing entities, and retain evidence about where facts came from. It will support questions such as “Which devices belong to users without MFA?” through a combination of explicit relationships and validated AI query planning.
    
    The planned API consists of:
    
    | Endpoint | Purpose |
    | --- | --- |
    | `POST /ingest` | Process structured inventory or unfamiliar input into CIs and relationships. |
    | `GET /devices`, `GET /users`, `GET /apps` | List typed CIs with filtering and pagination. |
    | `GET /ci/{id}` | Inspect a CI, its relationships, and supporting evidence. |
    | `POST /ask` | Answer natural-language questions using a constrained, read-only query plan. |
    
    ## Preview the sample data
    
    From the project directory, run all five supplied files and print their normalized output as JSON:
    
    ```sh
    .venv/bin/python -m app.ingestion
    ```
    
    To inspect one file or save the output:
    
    ```sh
    .venv/bin/python -m app.ingestion --file sample_hardware.yaml
    .venv/bin/python -m app.ingestion > /tmp/cmdb-output.json
    ```
    
    The output contains a summary and a separate normalized batch for each file, including attributes, identifiers, relationship assertions, and warnings. Add `--include-raw` to include original parsed records. This runs preparation only: records are not merged or written to a database, and no AI is called. It works without SQLAlchemy installed.
    
    The explicit sample source profile is in [examples/sample_sources.json](examples/sample_sources.json). Use `--config PATH` for another profile, `--input-dir PATH` for another input directory, or repeat `--file NAME` to select several configured files. Run `--help` for usage.
    
    ## Architecture
    
    Two workflows share the same relational model:
    
    ```mermaid
    flowchart TD
      I[Inventory input] --> E[Source adapter or AI extraction]
      E --> V[Validation and normalization]
      V --> R[Identity resolution and evidence policy]
      R --> DB[(CMDB)]
      Q[Natural-language question] --> P[AI-generated structured plan]
      P --> C[Validation and safe SQLAlchemy execution]
      C --> DB
      DB --> A[Grounded results and limitations]
    ```
    
    Recognized structured inputs use deterministic adapters. Unfamiliar input uses AI-assisted extraction into the same Pydantic-validated record format. New source layouts belong in adapters; source authority, identifier scopes, and aliases belong in configuration rather than sample-specific branches in core services.
    
    Entity resolution determines whether an incoming record describes an existing CI. It uses trusted identifiers, not similar names. Provenance records the source and observation supporting a fact so discrepancies remain explainable. These decisions happen in deterministic services after extraction, before transactional persistence.
    
    For natural-language queries, the model proposes a limited plan containing filters, counts, and at most two relationship hops. The application validates that plan and builds SQLAlchemy expressions using allowlisted fields and bound parameters. The model receives neither the entire database nor permission to execute arbitrary SQL. Responses are constructed from actual results and disclose relevant missing or conflicting evidence.
    
    Routes, database models, validation schemas, ingestion adapters, identity resolution, AI integration, and query execution will have separate responsibilities. Tests will inject an AI client so normal verification does not require provider access.
    
    ## Technology choices and tradeoffs
    
    | Technology | Why it fits | Tradeoff |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Python 3.12+ and FastAPI | A small REST backend with explicit request validation and generated API documentation. | Synchronous request processing keeps the prototype simple; long-running ingestion would eventually need background jobs. |
    | SQLAlchemy 2.x | Explicit models, transactions, and composable relational queries. | Requires deliberate schema design; database-specific concurrency behavior still needs testing. |
    | SQLite | Local persistence without a separate database service, with straightforward isolated tests. | Writes are serialized; unsuitable for a large concurrent ingestion workload. |
    | Pydantic v2 | Shared validation boundaries for HTTP requests, extracted records, and AI query plans. | Valid structure does not guarantee correct facts; identity and evidence checks remain necessary. |
    | OpenRouter | Configurable model access through a small HTTP client. | Adds external latency, cost, failure modes, and data-handling considerations. |
    | pytest | Focused policy tests and end-to-end API tests with mocked AI responses. | Mock tests need a separate optional live smoke test to check provider compatibility. |
    | Standard JSON/CSV parsers and safe PyYAML | Reliable parsing of recognized formats without an LLM call. | Source semantics still require adapters; matching syntax alone is insufficient. |
    
    ### Why a relational database?
    
    The main operations are exact identity lookups, attribute filtering, and short relationship traversals. Relational tables support these operations while enforcing identifier uniqueness, valid references, and atomic ingestion. A shared CI table also gives every relationship a consistent foreign-key target.
    
    A graph database could help with unrestricted deep traversal, but that is outside the prototype's query language. A document-only model would make cross-entity constraints and joins less direct. SQLite provides the relational behavior needed for a runnable local prototype without extra infrastructure.
    
    PostgreSQL is the intended production path if concurrent writes or operational requirements outgrow SQLite. SQLAlchemy preserves much of the model and query logic, but migrations, native column types, locking, and database-specific indexes would still need implementation and testing.
    
    ## Data model overview
    
    The schema separates identity, typed attributes, relationships, and evidence:
    
    | Layer | Planned tables | Responsibility |
    | --- | --- | --- |
    | Shared identity | `configuration_items`, `entity_identifiers` | Stable internal UUIDs and external keys scoped by organization, CI type, authority, and identifier type. |
    | Typed attributes | `devices`, `users`, `applications`, `user_groups` | Queryable properties and many-valued group membership. Each CI has exactly one matching subtype. |
    | Connections | `relationships` | Directed, typed assignment, access, dependency, integration, and human-owner edges. Team ownership remains an application attribute. |
    | Ingestion evidence | `ingestion_runs`, `observations` | Replay detection, source records, reliable observation times, unresolved references, and conflicting evidence. |
    
    Multiple external identifiers may point to one CI. If an incoming record's identifiers point to different CIs, the record is retained for review without merging or modifying those entities. Hostnames and IP addresses are not universally unique. Cross-source aliases and shared identifier authorities require explicit configuration.
    
    Conflicting attributes follow a small deterministic policy: prefer a configured attribute authority; otherwise use the latest reliable observation when competing evidence is comparable. If neither establishes a winner, preserve the candidates and expose the field as unresolved. File format and arrival order confer no priority, and activity times such as last_login do not timestamp inventory observations. Missing values never erase known facts.
    
    Unknown or conflicted MFA projects to NULL, while false means an explicit negative observation. CI details distinguish missing values from conflicts. Integrations remain distinct from dependencies, and reported application user totals remain distinct from observed access assignments.
    
    The [technical design](docs/design.md#4-data-model-and-entity-relationships) includes concrete columns, constraints, indexes, and separate diagrams for the core CMDB and ingestion evidence.
    
    ## Assumptions and limitations
    
    The prototype targets one configured organization per deployment. It accepts bounded uploads and supports the three CI types and defined relationship vocabulary; arbitrary source data must map into that model. New CI types or first-class queryable attributes require deliberate schema changes.
    
    Identity matching is conservative. Name-only references may remain unresolved, and similarly named users from different sources will not automatically merge. Consequently, some relationship queries may be incomplete even when a human suspects two records describe the same entity. Responses should report that limitation rather than invent a link.
    
    Access, groups, and most relationships are additive observations. Missing entries in later uploads do not revoke access. Current device assignment is single-valued and follows the evidence policy. Complete relationship history, automatic reconciliation, and snapshot revocation are deferred.
    
    Authentication, tenant authorization, bulk streaming, background workers, arbitrary SQL, unrestricted graph traversal, and automatic CI merging are outside the timebox. Production use would require access controls, provider data-handling review, evidence retention policies, backups, and stronger concurrent-write handling.
    
    The supplied files in [input_data/](input_data/) serve as adapter and integration fixtures. Their counts, aliases, and shared-source assumptions belong to test configuration, not core architecture. The [sample-data testing plan](docs/design.md#10-sample-data-and-integration-testing) documents those assumptions and expected outcomes.

Override `CMDB_DATABASE_URL` and `CMDB_SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` in the environment; [.env.example](.env.example) documents the defaults. No dotenv loader is installed. Tests use temporary or in-memory databases rather than the default database.

    ### Deterministic preparation (Phase 2)
    
    `app.ingestion.service.prepare_ingestion` accepts a validated `IngestRequest` and trusted `SourceConfig` objects. It returns a `PreparedIngestion` containing the normalized batch, source metadata, and bounded warnings. The function has no database or AI dependencies and does not persist or resolve entities.
    
    The built-in adapter IDs are `hardware_json`, `hardware_csv`, `hardware_yaml`, `okta_json`, and `applications_json`. Source configuration selects an adapter, identifier authorities, optional identifier case rules, and an optional trusted snapshot-time path. Serial and email identifiers require explicit configuration; external IDs otherwise remain source-local. New adapters can be registered without changing the preparation workflow.
    
    For example, using the supplied hardware JSON as a local parsing fixture:
    
    ```python
    from pathlib import Path
    
    from app.ingestion.service import prepare_ingestion
    from app.schemas.ingest import IngestRequest, SourceConfig
    
    source = SourceConfig(
        organization_id="demo-org", source_id="inventory-demo", adapter="hardware_json"
    )
    request = IngestRequest(
        organization_id="demo-org",
        source_id="inventory-demo",
        format="json",
        content=Path("input_data/sample_hardware.json").read_text(),
    )
    prepared = prepare_ingestion(request, [source])
    print(prepared.batch.model_dump_json(indent=2))
    ```
    
    Malformed known inputs fail without an AI fallback. Unknown descriptions produce warnings and unknown values, rather than guessed booleans. Preparation preserves parsed raw records and source paths, checks upload/record/relationship limits, rejects duplicate JSON/YAML keys and CSV headers, and rejects YAML aliases and unsafe tags. YAML dates remain text until explicitly normalized. The same limits apply to all configured sources; fixture counts and names are not service policy.
    
    Server startup, OpenRouter configuration, and persisted ingestion/query demonstrations will be documented when those phases exist. No HTTP server, identity resolver, reconciliation policy, or AI calls have been added.

Entity update counts reflect changed attributes, identifiers, or reference status; evidence-only additions count as unchanged entities. Relationship counts compare the affected current graph before and after processing, including retained edges.
        
        Configure policies before loading data. A policy change gives uploads a new replay version; deliberately reingest affected data to refresh its projections. Existing CIs are never automatically merged to accommodate a new alias. Policy migration and a reconciliation UI remain out of scope.
        
        Phase 3 uses SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` for short write transactions. All successful projections, relationship changes, quarantine evidence, and the run summary commit together. Contention returns retryable 503; unexpected errors roll back the run. Reference CIs can represent any supported type when a stable identifier exists; a name-only person never creates one. Conflicting connected identity groups are quarantined together to avoid input-order-dependent partial updates.
        
        No AI calls, unstructured extraction, `/ask`, access revocation, or historical graph queries are implemented yet.''')

    from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
    from uuid import uuid4
    
    from fastapi import FastAPI
    
    from app.api.errors import install_errors
    from app.api.ingest import router as ingest_router
    from app.api.inventory import router as inventory_router
    from app.config import Settings
    from app.db.session import create_sqlite_engine, initialize_database, session_factory
    from app.ingestion.persistence import IngestService
    from app.reconciliation.policy import Policy, load_sources
    
    
    def create_app(*, settings=None, sources=None, engine=None):
        settings = settings or Settings.from_env()
        sources = load_sources(settings.source_config_path) if sources is None else sources
        if any(source.organization_id != settings.organization_id for source in sources):
            raise ValueError("All sources must belong to the configured organization")
        policy = Policy(sources)
        owns_engine = engine is None
        engine = engine or create_sqlite_engine(settings)
    
        @asynccontextmanager
        async def lifespan(app):
            initialize_database(engine)
            try:
                yield
            finally:
                if owns_engine:
                    engine.dispose()
    
        app = FastAPI(title="AI-first CMDB", version="0.3.0", lifespan=lifespan)
        app.state.settings = settings
        app.state.sessions = session_factory(engine)
        app.state.ingestion = IngestService(app.state.sessions, policy)
    
        @app.middleware("http")
        async def correlation_id(request, call_next):
            request.state.request_id = str(uuid4())
            response = await call_next(request)
            response.headers["X-Request-ID"] = request.state.request_id
            return response
    
        install_errors(app)
        app.include_router(ingest_router)
        app.include_router(inventory_router)
        return app
    
    
    app = create_app()

    from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping, Sequence
    from typing import Any
    
    from pydantic import ValidationError
    
    from app.ingestion.adapters.applications import applications_json
    from app.ingestion.adapters.common import Context
    from app.ingestion.adapters.hardware import hardware_csv, hardware_json, hardware_yaml
    from app.ingestion.adapters.okta import okta_json
    from app.ingestion.errors import InputError
    from app.ingestion.parsing import parse_content
    from app.schemas.ingest import IngestRequest, PreparedIngestion, SourceConfig
    from app.schemas.normalized import NormalizedBatch
    
    # Adapter IDs describe layouts, not trusted identity domains or source rankings.
    # A new layout adds one function/registration without changing this workflow.
    Adapter = Callable[[Any, Context], tuple[list, dict]]
    ADAPTERS: dict[str, tuple[str, Adapter]] = {
        "hardware_json": ("json", hardware_json),
        "hardware_csv": ("csv", hardware_csv),
        "hardware_yaml": ("yaml", hardware_yaml),
        "okta_json": ("json", okta_json),
        "applications_json": ("json", applications_json),
    }
    
    
    def prepare_ingestion(
        request: IngestRequest,
        sources: Sequence[SourceConfig],
        *,
        adapters: Mapping[str, tuple[str, Adapter]] | None = None,
    ) -> PreparedIngestion:
        """Produce a complete validated batch; errors never return partial records.
    
        Unknown/unfamiliar layouts are explicit errors until Phase 4. Source config
        is supplied by trusted application code, never taken from the upload content.
        """
        index = {(source.organization_id, source.source_id): source for source in sources}
        if len(index) != len(sources):
            raise ValueError("Duplicate source configuration")
        source = index.get((request.organization_id, request.source_id))
        if source is None:
            raise InputError("Unknown source or organization", path="/source_id", code="unknown_source")
        selected = (ADAPTERS if adapters is None else adapters).get(source.adapter)
        if selected is None:
            raise InputError("No deterministic adapter configured", code="unsupported_source")
        format, adapter = selected
        if request.format != format:
            raise InputError("Format does not match configured source adapter", path="/format")
        document = parse_content(request.content, format)
        ctx = Context(source)
        ctx.snapshot(document)
        try:
            normalized, metadata = adapter(document, ctx)
            if len(normalized) > 1000:
                raise InputError("More than 1000 extracted entity records", code="limit_exceeded")
            batch = NormalizedBatch(records=normalized)
        except ValidationError as exc:
            # Retain only the field path, not Pydantic's potentially sensitive input values.
            location = "/".join(str(part) for part in exc.errors()[0]["loc"])
            raise InputError("Record does not satisfy the normalized schema", path=ctx.record_path.rstrip("/") + "/" + location) from exc
        return PreparedIngestion(organization_id=request.organization_id, source_id=request.source_id,
                                 batch=batch, source_metadata=metadata,
                                 warning_count=ctx.warning_count, warnings=ctx.warnings)

    from typing import Literal, Self
    
    from pydantic import Field, JsonValue, field_validator, model_validator
    
    from app.identity.namespaces import IdentifierScope
    from app.schemas.normalized import Contract, NormalizedBatch, Text
    
    
    class IngestRequest(Contract):
        organization_id: Text
        source_id: Text
        format: Literal["json", "csv", "yaml", "text"]
        content: str = Field(min_length=1)
    
        @field_validator("content")
        @classmethod
        def nonblank_content(cls, value: str) -> str:
            if not value.strip():
                raise ValueError("Content must not be blank")
            return value
    
    
    class SourceConfig(Contract):
        organization_id: Text
        source_id: Text
        adapter: Text
        # Unconfigured external IDs are source-local. Serial/email keys are opt-in.
        identifier_authorities: dict[str, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
        case_insensitive_identifiers: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: ["app_name"])
        application_aliases: dict[Text, Text] = Field(default_factory=dict)
        authoritative_attributes: list[Text] = Field(default_factory=list)
        snapshot_time_path: list[Text] | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=16)
    
        @model_validator(mode="after")
        def valid_scopes_and_snapshot(self) -> Self:
            IdentifierScope(organization_id=self.organization_id, ci_type="device",
                            authority_id=self.source_id, identifier_type="external_id")
            for key, authority in self.identifier_authorities.items():
                IdentifierScope(organization_id=self.organization_id, ci_type="device",
                                authority_id=authority, identifier_type=key)
            if self.snapshot_time_path and any(
                part.casefold() in {"last_login", "last_checkin"} for part in self.snapshot_time_path
            ):
                raise ValueError("Activity timestamps cannot be configured as snapshot times")
            return self
    
    
    class IngestWarning(Contract):
        code: str
        path: str
        message: str
    
    
    class PreparedIngestion(Contract):
        organization_id: str
        source_id: str
        batch: NormalizedBatch
        source_metadata: dict[str, JsonValue] = Field(default_factory=dict)
        warning_count: int
        warnings: list[IngestWarning]

    Kind = Literal["device", "user", "application"]

            if self.pointer is None and self.quote is None:
                raise ValueError("Evidence requires a source pointer or quote")
            return self
    
    
    class DeviceAttributes(Contract):
        hostname: Text | None = None
        ip_address: Text | None = None
        mac_address: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(pattern=r"^(?:[0-9A-F]{2}:){5}[0-9A-F]{2}$")] | None = None
        serial_number: Text | None = None
        os_family: Text | None = None
        os_version: Text | None = None
        location: Text | None = None
        status: Literal["active", "inactive", "unknown"] | None = None
        encrypted: bool | None = None
        device_type: Text | None = None
        department: Text | None = None
        last_checkin: AwareDatetime | None = None
    
        @field_validator("ip_address")
        @classmethod
        def valid_ip(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
            if value is not None:
                ip_address(value)
            return value
    
    
    class UserAttributes(Contract):
        name: Text | None = None
        email: Text | None = None
        team: Text | None = None
        department: Text | None = None
        title: Text | None = None
        status: Literal["active", "inactive", "suspended", "unknown"] | None = None
        mfa_enabled: bool | None = None
        last_login: AwareDatetime | None = None
        groups: list[Text] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=100)
    
        @field_validator("email")
        @classmethod
        def valid_email(cls, value: str | None) -> str | None:
            # A deliberately modest inventory-address check; no delivery verification.
            if value is not None:
                if value.count("@") != 1 or any(c.isspace() for c in value):
                    raise ValueError("Expected an email address")
                local, domain = value.split("@")
                if not local or not domain or domain.startswith(".") or domain.endswith("."):
                    raise ValueError("Expected an email address")
            return value
    
    
    class ApplicationAttributes(Contract):
        name: Text | None = None
        app_type: Literal["saas", "on_prem", "unknown"] | None = None
        vendor: Text | None = None
        category: Text | None = None
        deployment: Text | None = None
        owner_team: Text | None = None
        reported_user_count: Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)] | None = None
        sso_enabled: bool | None = None
    
    
    class EntityReference(Contract):
        ci_type: Kind
        identifiers: list[Identifier] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)
        display_name: Text | None = None
        evidence: Evidence | None = None
    
        @model_validator(mode="after")
        def identifier_types_match(self) -> Self:
            if any(i.scope.ci_type != self.ci_type for i in self.identifiers):
                raise ValueError("Reference identifiers must match the target CI type")
            if not self.identifiers and self.display_name is None:
                raise ValueError("Reference requires identifiers or an unresolved display name")
            return self
    
    
    class RelationshipAssertion(Contract):
        relation_type: Relation
        target: EntityReference
        evidence: Evidence | None = None
    
    
    class Record(Contract):
        ci_type: Kind
        record_key: Text
        organization_id: Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.:-]{0,127}$")]
        display_name: Text | None = None
        identifiers: list[Identifier] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=20)
        observed_at: AwareDatetime | None = None
        relationships: list[RelationshipAssertion] = Field(default_factory=list, max_length=5000)
        evidence: Evidence | None = None
        raw_record: JsonValue = None
    
        @model_validator(mode="after")
        def scopes_and_edges_match(self) -> Self:
            for identifier in self.identifiers:
                if (identifier.scope.organization_id, identifier.scope.ci_type) != (
                    self.organization_id, self.ci_type
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Identifier scope must match the record organization and type")
            for edge in self.relationships:
                validate_endpoints(edge.relation_type, self.ci_type, edge.target.ci_type)
                for identifier in edge.target.identifiers:
                    if identifier.scope.organization_id != self.organization_id:
                        raise ValueError("Relationship targets must share the record organization")
            return self
    
    
    class DeviceRecord(Record):
        ci_type: Literal["device"] = "device"
        attributes: DeviceAttributes
    
    
    class UserRecord(Record):
        ci_type: Literal["user"] = "user"
        attributes: UserAttributes
    
    
    class ApplicationRecord(Record):
        ci_type: Literal["application"] = "application"
        attributes: ApplicationAttributes
    
    
    NormalizedRecord = Annotated[
        DeviceRecord | UserRecord | ApplicationRecord, Field(discriminator="ci_type")
    ]
    
    
    class NormalizedBatch(Contract):
        records: list[NormalizedRecord] = Field(min_length=1, max_length=1000)
    
        @model_validator(mode="after")
        def bounded_unique_records(self) -> Self:
            keys = [record.record_key for record in self.records]
            if len(keys) != len(set(keys)):
                raise ValueError("Record paths must be unique within a batch")
            if sum(len(record.relationships) for record in self.records) > 5000:
                raise ValueError("At most 5000 relationship assertions are allowed per batch")
            if len({record.organization_id for record in self.records}) != 1:
                raise ValueError("One batch must belong to one organization")
            return self
    """Bounded strict readers for JSON, CSV and safe YAML."""
    
    import csv
    import io
    import json
    import math
    from typing import Any
    
    import yaml
    
    from app.ingestion.errors import InputError
    
    MAX_BYTES = 1024 * 1024
    MAX_DEPTH = 32
    MAX_NODES = 100000
    MAX_RECORDS = 1000
    
    
    def _unique_object(pairs):
        result = {}
        for key, value in pairs:
            if key in result:
                raise InputError("Duplicate mapping key")
            result[key] = value
        return result
    
    
    class InventoryLoader(yaml.SafeLoader):
        """Reject aliases rather than expanding untrusted YAML graphs."""
    
        def __init__(self, stream):
            super().__init__(stream)
            self.inventory_depth = 0
            self.inventory_nodes = 0
    
        def compose_node(self, parent, index):
            if self.check_event(yaml.AliasEvent):
                raise InputError("YAML aliases are not supported")
            self.inventory_depth += 1
            self.inventory_nodes += 1
            if self.inventory_depth > MAX_DEPTH or self.inventory_nodes > MAX_NODES:
                raise InputError("YAML nesting or node limit exceeded", code="limit_exceeded")
            try:
                return super().compose_node(parent, index)
            finally:
                self.inventory_depth -= 1
    
        def construct_mapping(self, node, deep=False):
            pairs = []
            for key_node, value_node in node.value:
                key = self.construct_object(key_node, deep=deep)
                if not isinstance(key, str):
                    raise InputError("Mapping keys must be strings")
                pairs.append((key, self.construct_object(value_node, deep=deep)))
            return _unique_object(pairs)
    
    
    # Preserve date spelling as text; semantic timestamp validation happens explicitly.
    InventoryLoader.yaml_implicit_resolvers = {
        key: [(tag, regex) for tag, regex in values if tag != "tag:yaml.org,2002:timestamp"]
        for key, values in yaml.SafeLoader.yaml_implicit_resolvers.items()
    }
    
    
    def _check_tree(data: Any) -> None:
        stack = [(data, 0)]
        nodes = 0
        while stack:
            value, depth = stack.pop()
            nodes += 1
            if depth > MAX_DEPTH or nodes > MAX_NODES:
                raise InputError("Document nesting or node limit exceeded", code="limit_exceeded")
            if isinstance(value, dict):
                if any(not isinstance(key, str) for key in value):
                    raise InputError("Mapping keys must be strings")
                for key in value:
                    try:
                        key.encode("utf-8")
                    except UnicodeError as exc:
                        raise InputError("Mapping keys must be valid UTF-8 text") from exc
                stack.extend((child, depth + 1) for child in value.values())
            elif isinstance(value, list):
                stack.extend((child, depth + 1) for child in value)
            elif isinstance(value, str):
                try:
                    value.encode("utf-8")
                except UnicodeError as exc:
                    raise InputError("Source strings must be valid UTF-8 text") from exc
            elif isinstance(value, float) and not math.isfinite(value):
                raise InputError("Non-finite numbers are not supported")
            elif value is not None and not isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bool)):
                raise InputError("Unsupported source value type")
    
    
    def parse_content(content: str, format: str) -> Any:
        try:
            size = len(content.encode("utf-8"))
        except UnicodeError as exc:
            raise InputError("Content must be valid UTF-8 text") from exc
        if size > MAX_BYTES:
            raise InputError("Upload exceeds 1 MiB", code="limit_exceeded")
        try:
            if format == "json":
                data = json.loads(content, object_pairs_hook=_unique_object)
            elif format == "yaml":
                data = yaml.load(content, Loader=InventoryLoader)
            elif format == "csv":
                reader = csv.reader(io.StringIO(content, newline=""), strict=True)
                headers = next(reader, None)
                if not headers:
                    raise InputError("CSV requires a header")
                headers = [header.strip().removeprefix("\ufeff") for header in headers]
                if any(not h for h in headers) or len(headers) != len(set(headers)):
                    raise InputError("CSV headers must be nonblank and unique")
                data = []
                for row in reader:
                    if not row:  # Empty physical lines are not inventory records.
                        continue
                    if len(row) != len(headers):
                        raise InputError("CSV row length does not match header", path=f"/rows/{len(data)}")
                    if len(data) == MAX_RECORDS:
                        raise InputError("More than 1000 records", code="limit_exceeded")
                    data.append(dict(zip(headers, row)))
                # Headers remain available even if the document contains zero rows.
                return {"headers": headers, "rows": data}
            else:
                raise InputError("No deterministic adapter for this format", code="unsupported_format")
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, yaml.YAMLError, csv.Error, RecursionError) as exc:
            raise InputError("Malformed input document") from exc
        _check_tree(data)
        return data
