    YAML hardware users have emails [john.doe@example.com](mailto:john.doe@example.com), [jane.doe@example.com](mailto:jane.doe@example.com), and [sarah.chen@example.com](mailto:sarah.chen@example.com); similarly named Okta accounts use [john.d@example.com](mailto:john.d@example.com), [jane.d@example.com](mailto:jane.d@example.com), and [s.chen@example.com](mailto:s.chen@example.com). No supplied stable identifier bridges those pairs. The tests must preserve separate users rather than manufacture joins.
    
    ### Explicit test configuration
    
    The fixture configuration declares one organization and maps the three hardware exports' device IDs to a common inventory authority. This tests the assumption that their repeated IDs are from one inventory; core services do not infer that from filenames. Separate source instances select the appropriate adapters.
    
    An optional alias-enabled test profile declares a shared application catalog-name authority, with GitHub → GitHub Enterprise and Salesforce → Salesforce CRM. These aliases represent reviewed fixture assumptions and live entirely in test configuration. Test an empty alias configuration too: cross-source labels remain separate unless their declared authority guarantees a match. No application-specific branch belongs in the resolver.
    
    The baseline test profile designates **no attribute authority**. Only YAML and the app inventory have reliable snapshot timestamps; JSON and CSV hardware check-ins cannot substitute for them. Thus incomparable contradictory device statuses remain conflicted. With all three hardware files loaded, John's and Jane's status fields project to NULL, Sarah's active state agrees across sources, and the active-device count is **one with two conflicted statuses disclosed**. A timestamped observation cannot defeat an undated contradictory value under the baseline policy.
    
    A separate test profile may designate the YAML source instance authoritative for device status and location. Under that configuration John's state is inactive and Jane/Sarah active, so the active count becomes two. This tests configured **source authority**, not YAML's file format. The same authority behavior must hold when a synthetic authoritative source supplies JSON or CSV.
    
    ### Expected integration outcomes
    
    With shared hardware authority and the alias-enabled profile, expect 3 devices, 12 users (9 Okta plus 3 hardware), and 28 applications including reference-only CIs. Expect 3 identified device assignments, 25 uses edges, and 16 directed integration edges. Name-only hardware assignment observations remain unresolved evidence and do not create extra users or replace identified assignments. There are no supported facts establishing dependency edges or human application owners.
    
    Required ask tests include three MFA-false users, two macOS devices, five GitHub users, and the configured active-device result above. Device-to-MFA joins return no matches because the hardware users' MFA is unknown and their similarly named Okta counterparts are not merged. Responses must disclose the identity/MFA coverage gap. Dependency queries return no recorded edges and a missing-evidence notice; integrations cannot supply an answer to dependency questions.
    
    Test order independence, exact replay, equivalent reformatted uploads, reference enrichment, duplicate hostnames, conflicting device ID/serial matches, missing identifiers, and preserved conflicting values. Use synthetic records for positive two-hop MFA/app queries, dependencies, human ownership, and equal-time conflicts; the provided inputs cannot prove those paths work. Synthetic authority/freshness tests must also show that last_login, last_checkin, and arrival time never select a winner.
    
    ## 11. Implementation roadmap
    
    The structure should reflect responsibilities without creating a framework around every function:
    
    ```text
    app/
      main.py
      config.py
      api/              # ingest, inventory, ask routes
      db/               # models and sessions
      schemas/          # API, normalized records, query plans
      ingestion/        # service, normalization, source adapters
      identity/         # namespace construction, resolver, aliases
      ai/               # OpenRouter client, extraction, planning prompts
      querying/         # registry, compiler, answer templates
    tests/
      unit/
      integration/
      fixtures/         # synthetic inputs and fixture configuration
    input_data/         # supplied files, unchanged
    requirements.txt
    pytest.ini
    .env.example
    README.md
    ```
    
    
    | Phase                                | Work and completion gate                                                                                                                       | Required verification                                                                                                                                               | Budget |
    | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
    | 1. Models and contracts              | Project skeleton, settings, SQLite session, tables, Pydantic normalized contract.                                                              | Key/FK constraints, nullable MFA, subtype checks, typed edges, assignment uniqueness.                                                                               | 50 min |
    | 2. Deterministic ingestion           | Adapters for every supplied structure, common normalization, envelope validation.                                                              | All five files map correctly; malformed structure and false/unknown cases covered.                                                                                  | 60 min |
    | 3. Identity, evidence, relationships | Namespaces, aliases, resolution/quarantine, authority/freshness selection, transactional upsert/replay, list/detail routes.                    | Duplicate keys, conflicting identities, missing keys, order-independent projections, preserved conflicts, edge deduplication, expected configured fixture outcomes. | 90 min |
    | 4. AI extraction                     | Injected OpenRouter client, schema/evidence validation, bounded retry.                                                                         | Mock valid/invalid outputs, invented identifiers, timeout, failure without writes.                                                                                  | 30 min |
    | 5. Natural-language planning         | Limited plan schema and prompt, unsupported/clarification branches.                                                                            | Plans for required question patterns, invalid fields/types/depth, ambiguous names, injection attempts.                                                              | 30 min |
    | 6. Query execution                   | EXISTS compiler, counts, pagination, answer templates, focused evidence warnings.                                                              | Same-person nested semantics, NULL versus false, distinct root counts, positive synthetic dependency/two-hop cases.                                                 | 50 min |
    | 7. Integration testing               | End-to-end API flow and rollback/error contracts on temporary SQLite.                                                                          | Fixture permutations, replay, quarantine, transaction rollback, uniform errors; optional live AI smoke test.                                                        | 40 min |
    | 8. Documentation/demo                | Update planned status to actual capabilities, reproducible setup/launch/test commands, ingest/query demo, sanitized AI-development transcript. | Fresh-environment demo and README examples match actual responses.                                                                                                  | 25 min |
    
    
    Total: **6 hours 15 minutes**, leaving 45–105 minutes within the assignment window. The riskiest work is identity/evidence handling, so it gets the largest block. Avoid adding a reconciliation UI, general history engine, or elaborate retry machinery. If integration takes longer, reduce optional extracted attributes and presentation polish rather than skipping core ingest/query behavior or tests.
    
    The README now includes dependency installation, environment settings, database initialization, server launch, pytest, and a reproducible ingestion demonstration. AI setup, raw-upload examples, and natural-language query examples are documented. Delivery remains private as the assignment requests. AI-development documentation should describe actual assistance and include sanitized transcripts; this design was prepared with Codex from the assignment and local files.
    
    **Next planned phases:** broader integration verification and final documentation/demo. Planning, deterministic execution, and grounded answers are complete, including a preview API and CLI. Extraction already uses the shared validated-record and transactional persistence boundaries.
    
    ## 12. Limitations and production considerations
    
    
    
    ### Planned prototype versus deferred work
    
    The planned prototype includes the six endpoints, configurable source/identity policies, supplied-format adapters, AI extraction for unfamiliar content, deterministic identity resolution, lightweight evidence/conflict flags, idempotent ingestion, typed relationships, and validated natural-language plans with bounded execution. Phases 1–6 supply models, preparation/extraction, identity/evidence reconciliation, transactional persistence, and inventory HTTP routes. Database, HTTP, and mocked-provider tests run successfully. Live provider connectivity remains unverified; natural-language planning and execution are implemented.
    
    It intentionally excludes authentication, tenant authorization, fuzzy identity matching, automatic CI merging, historical graph queries, relationship revocation, streaming uploads, background jobs, arbitrary graph traversal, cost analytics, and full normalization of every source field. Additive access/group/integration data can become stale; responses describe observed evidence rather than a live authoritative directory. Unresolved records are retained and counted, but there is no reconciliation browser in this timebox.
    
    ### Production path
    
    Larger datasets would use object storage, asynchronous jobs, batch identifier lookups, and checkpointed processing. Chunked commits would need an explicit job/partial-progress contract; they must not silently replace the current request-atomic behavior. Evidence retention and pruning also become necessary as observations accumulate.

    from app.db.models import Application, ConfigurationItem, Device, IngestionRun, Observation, Relationship, User
    from app.db.session import session_factory
    from app.ingestion.persistence import IngestService

    ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
    
    
    def source(name="inventory", adapter="hardware_json", **changes):
        return SourceConfig(organization_id="org-a", source_id=name, adapter=adapter, **changes)
    
    
    def request(data, src="inventory", format="json", org="org-a"):
        return IngestRequest(organization_id=org, source_id=src, format=format,
                             content=data if isinstance(data, str) else json.dumps(data))
    
    
    def test_replay_and_semantic_duplicates(engine):
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([source()]))
        req = request([{"device_id": "D1", "hostname": "host"}])
        first = service.ingest(req)
        second = service.ingest(req)
        assert first["entities"]["created"] == 1
        assert second == first | {"replayed": True}
        service.ingest(req.model_copy(update={"content": json.dumps(json.loads(req.content), indent=2)}))
        with sessions() as db:
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(ConfigurationItem)) == 1
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(IngestionRun)) == 2
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Observation)) == 2
    
    
    def test_attribute_conflicts_preserved_and_quarantine_is_committed(engine):
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([source()]))
        result = service.ingest(request([{"device_id": "D1", "status": "active"},
                                         {"device_id": "D1", "status": "inactive"},
                                         {"hostname": "no-stable-key"}]))
        assert result["records"] == {"received": 3, "resolved": 2, "quarantined": 1}
        with sessions() as db:
            ci = db.scalar(select(Device))
            assert ci.status is None
            assert ci.field_state["status"]["status"] == "conflict"
            assert len(ci.field_state["status"]["observation_ids"]) == 2
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Observation)) == 3
    
    
    def test_identity_conflict_cannot_partially_update_attributes(engine):
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        cfg = source(identifier_authorities={"serial": "serials"})
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([cfg]))
        service.ingest(request([{"device_id": "D1", "serial_number": "S1", "hostname": "one"},
                                {"device_id": "D2", "serial_number": "S2", "hostname": "two"}]))
        outcome = service.ingest(request([{"device_id": "D1", "serial_number": "S2", "hostname": "incorrect"}]))
        assert outcome["records"]["quarantined"] == 1
        with sessions() as db:
            assert set(db.scalars(select(Device.hostname))) == {"one", "two"}
            conflict = db.scalar(select(Observation).where(Observation.resolution_status == "identity_conflict"))
            assert conflict.ci_id is None
            assert len(conflict.normalized_record["candidate_ids"]) == 2
    
    
    def test_authority_and_freshness_are_source_configuration(engine):
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        a = source("a", authoritative_attributes=["device.status"], identifier_authorities={"device_id": "shared"})
        b = source("b", identifier_authorities={"device_id": "shared"})
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([a, b]))
        service.ingest(request([{"device_id": "D", "status": "active"}], "a"))
        service.ingest(request([{"device_id": "D", "status": "inactive"}], "b"))
        service.ingest(request([{"device_id": "D", "status": None}], "a"))
        with sessions() as db:
            assert db.scalar(select(Device.status)) == "active"
    
    
    def test_entire_write_rolls_back_on_failure(engine, monkeypatch):
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([source()]))
        import app.ingestion.persistence as module
        def fail(*args):
            raise RuntimeError("Injected projection failure")
        monkeypatch.setattr(module, "project_relationships", fail)
        with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="Injected"):
            service.ingest(request([{"device_id": "D1", "hostname": "host"}]))
        with sessions() as db:
            for model in (ConfigurationItem, IngestionRun, Observation, Relationship):
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(model)) == 0
    
    
    def sample_sources():
        sources = load_sources(ROOT / "examples/sample_sources.json")
        for src in sources:
            if src.adapter in {"okta_json", "applications_json"}:
                src.application_aliases = {"GitHub": "GitHub Enterprise", "Salesforce": "Salesforce CRM"}
        return sources
    
    
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("reverse", [False, True])
    def test_all_sample_files_and_order_independent_conflicts(engine, reverse):
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        sources = sample_sources()
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy(sources))
        manifest = json.loads((ROOT / "examples/sample_sources.json").read_text())
        for entry in manifest[::-1] if reverse else manifest:
            cfg = next(s for s in sources if s.source_id == entry["source"]["source_id"])
            formats = {"hardware_yaml": "yaml", "hardware_csv": "csv"}
            req = request((ROOT / "input_data" / entry["file"]).read_text(), cfg.source_id,
                          formats.get(cfg.adapter, "json"), cfg.organization_id)
            result = service.ingest(req)
            assert result["records"]["quarantined"] == 0
        with sessions() as db:
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Device)) == 3
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(User)) == 12
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Application)) == 28
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Relationship).where(Relationship.relation_type == "uses")) == 25
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Relationship).where(Relationship.relation_type == "integrates_with")) == 16
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Relationship).where(Relationship.relation_type == "assigned_to")) == 3
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Device).where(Device.status == "active")) == 1
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Device).where(Device.status.is_(None))) == 2
    
    
    def test_reliable_snapshot_time_selects_latest_even_when_ingested_first(engine):
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        cfg = source("apps", adapter="applications_json", snapshot_time_path=["inventory_metadata", "export_date"])
        # Catalog counts are attributes; only the explicitly configured export time orders observations.
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([cfg]))

                                    "applications": [{"app_id": "A", "users_count": count}]}, "apps"))

    def test_assignment_replacement_and_conflict_preserve_evidence(engine):
        from app.schemas.ingest import PreparedIngestion
        from app.schemas.normalized import NormalizedBatch
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        cfg = source()
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([cfg]))
        def prepared(target, observed):
            scope = dict(organization_id="org-a", ci_type="device", authority_id="inventory", identifier_type="device_id")
            user_scope = scope | {"ci_type": "user", "identifier_type": "user_id"}
            return PreparedIngestion(organization_id="org-a", source_id="inventory", warning_count=0, warnings=[],
                batch=NormalizedBatch.model_validate_json(json.dumps({"records": [{
                    "ci_type": "device", "organization_id": "org-a", "record_key": "/0", "attributes": {},
                    "observed_at": observed, "identifiers": [{"scope": scope, "value": "D"}],
                    "relationships": [{"relation_type": "assigned_to", "target": {
                        "ci_type": "user", "identifiers": [{"scope": user_scope, "value": target}]}}]
                }]})))
        service.persist(request("first"), prepared("U1", "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"))
        result = service.persist(request("second"), prepared("U2", "2025-01-02T00:00:00Z"))
        assert result["relationships"]["removed"] == 1
        assert result["relationships"]["created"] == 1
        # An undated contradictory assertion makes the current assignment unknown.
        result = service.persist(request("third"), prepared("U1", None))
        assert result["relationships"]["removed"] == 1
        with sessions() as db:
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Relationship)) == 0
            device = db.scalar(select(Device))
            assert device.field_state["assigned_to"]["status"] == "conflict"
            assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Observation).where(
                Observation.normalized_record["record_kind"].as_string() == "relationship")) == 3

        first = IngestService(sessions, Policy([cfg])).ingest(request([{"device_id": "D", "status": "active"}]))

    def test_concurrent_exact_replay_has_one_committed_run(tmp_path):
        from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
        from app.config import Settings
        from app.db.session import create_sqlite_engine, initialize_database
        engine = create_sqlite_engine(Settings(database_url=f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'concurrent.db'}"))
        initialize_database(engine)
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        service = IngestService(sessions, Policy([source()]))
        req = request([{"device_id": "D"}])
        try:
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=2) as pool:
                results = list(pool.map(lambda _: service.ingest(req), range(2)))
            assert {r["replayed"] for r in results} == {False, True}
            assert len({r["run_id"] for r in results}) == 1
            with sessions() as db:
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(IngestionRun)) == 1
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Device)) == 1
        finally:
            engine.dispose()
    
    
    def test_database_lock_is_a_retryable_error(tmp_path):
        from app.config import Settings
        from app.db.session import create_sqlite_engine, initialize_database
        from app.ingestion.persistence import DatabaseBusy
        engine = create_sqlite_engine(Settings(database_url=f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'locked.db'}", sqlite_busy_timeout_ms=1))
        initialize_database(engine)
        sessions = session_factory(engine)
        try:
            with engine.connect().execution_options(sqlite_write=True) as connection:
                transaction = connection.begin()
                with pytest.raises(DatabaseBusy):
                    IngestService(sessions, Policy([source()])).ingest(request([{"device_id": "D"}]))
                transaction.rollback()
            with sessions() as db:
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(IngestionRun)) == 0
        finally:
            engine.dispose()

    class FakeClient:
        def __init__(self, outputs):
            self.settings = Settings()
            self.outputs = list(outputs)
            self.calls = 0
            self.hook = None
    
        def complete(self, **kwargs):
            if self.hook:
                self.hook()
            index = min(self.calls, len(self.outputs) - 1)
            self.calls += 1
            value = self.outputs[index]
            if isinstance(value, Exception):
                raise value
            return value if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value)

    def add_upload_source(sources, organization):
        sources = list(sources)
        automatic = next((source for source in sources if source.adapter == "auto"), None)
        if automatic is not None:
            return sources, automatic.source_id
        source_id = "uploaded-data"
        while any(s.source_id == source_id for s in sources):
            source_id += "-auto"
        sources.append(SourceConfig(organization_id=organization, source_id=source_id, adapter="auto",
                                    identifier_authorities={"email": source_id},
                                    case_insensitive_identifiers=["email", "app_name"]))
        return sources, source_id
    
    
    def decode_content(data):
        try:
            content = data.decode("utf-8-sig")
        except UnicodeError:
            raise InputError("Use a UTF-8 JSON, CSV, YAML, or text file; binary uploads are not supported.",
                             code="unsupported_encoding", path="/file") from None
        if "\x00" in content or content.startswith(("%PDF-", "PK\x03\x04")):
            raise InputError("Binary files such as PDF/Excel/images are unsupported. Export JSON, CSV, YAML, or text.",
                             code="unsupported_file", path="/file")
        if not content.strip():
            raise InputError("The uploaded file or text is empty.", path="/content")
        return content
    
    
    def create_ingest_router(sources, default_source):
        router = APIRouter(tags=["Ingestion"])
        SourceChoice = Enum("IngestSource", {f"SOURCE_{i}": source.source_id for i, source in enumerate(sources)}, type=str)
        by_id = {s.source_id: s for s in sources}
        source_description = (
            "Choose a configured source, or " + default_source + " for automatic layout detection and AI extraction. "
            "Organization and known-source format are derived from server configuration."
        )
        multipart_schema = dict(type="object", required=["file"], properties={
            "file": {"type": "string", "format": "binary", "description": "UTF-8 inventory file, at most 1 MiB."},
            "source_id": {"type": "string", "enum": list(by_id), "default": default_source, "description": source_description},
            "format": {"type": "string", "enum": ["auto", *FORMATS], "default": "auto",
                       "description": "Usually leave auto. Known sources determine their format."},
        })
    
        def raw_request(content, source_id, format="auto", *, filename=None, media_type=None):
            source = by_id.get(source_id)
            if source is None:
                raise InputError("Unknown source. Use GET /ingest/sources to list configured choices.", path="/source_id", code="unknown_source")
            if format not in ("auto", *FORMATS):
                raise InputError("Format must be auto, json, csv, yaml, or text.", path="/format")
            known = ADAPTERS.get(source.adapter)
            if known is not None:
                if format not in ("auto", known[0]):
                    raise InputError(f"Selected source expects {known[0]}; leave format auto or choose a different source.", path="/format")
                format = known[0]
            elif format == "auto":
                format = detect_format(content, filename=filename, media_type=media_type)
            try:
                return IngestRequest(organization_id=source.organization_id, source_id=source.source_id,
                                     format=format, content=content)
            except ValidationError as exc:
                raise InputError("Invalid raw input; check the selected source and format.") from exc
    
        async def submit(request, payload):
            if payload.organization_id != request.app.state.settings.organization_id:
                raise InputError("Unknown source or organization", code="unknown_source", path="/organization_id")
            return await run_in_threadpool(request.app.state.ingestion.ingest, payload)

    class AIError(RuntimeError):
        def __init__(self, message, *, code="ai_invalid_response", status_code=502):
            super().__init__(message)
            self.code = code
            self.status_code = status_code
    
    
    class OpenRouterClient:
        ENDPOINT = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions"
    
        def __init__(self, settings, *, transport=None):
            self.settings = settings
            self.transport = transport
    
        def _key(self):
            if self.settings.openrouter_api_key is not None:
                value = self.settings.openrouter_api_key.get_secret_value().strip()
            else:
                try:
                    value = Path(self.settings.openrouter_token_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
                except (OSError, UnicodeError):
                    raise AIError("OpenRouter is not configured. Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY or provide token.txt.",
                                  code="ai_unavailable", status_code=503) from None
            if not value or not value.isascii() or any(character.isspace() for character in value):
                raise AIError("OpenRouter credentials must contain one nonempty API key.", code="ai_unavailable", status_code=503)
            return value
    
        def complete(self, *, messages, schema, schema_name="cmdb_extraction"):
            key = self._key()
            if not key:
                raise AIError("OpenRouter API key is empty.", code="ai_unavailable", status_code=503)
            payload = dict(model=self.settings.openrouter_model, messages=messages, temperature=0,
                           max_tokens=self.settings.openrouter_max_tokens, provider={"require_parameters": True},
                           response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {
                               "name": schema_name, "strict": False, "schema": schema}})
            try:
                with httpx.Client(timeout=self.settings.openrouter_timeout_seconds, transport=self.transport) as client:
                    with client.stream("POST", self.ENDPOINT, headers={
                        "Authorization": "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json",
                    }, json=payload) as response:
                        if response.status_code in (401, 402, 403, 429) or response.status_code >= 500:
                            raise AIError("OpenRouter is unavailable, rate-limited, or could not authorize the request.",
                                          code="ai_unavailable", status_code=503)
                        if response.status_code != 200:
                            raise AIError("OpenRouter rejected the model request; check the model/schema settings or use a smaller input.")
                        chunks, size = [], 0
                        for chunk in response.iter_bytes():
                            size += len(chunk)
                            if size > 1024 * 1024:
                                raise AIError("OpenRouter response exceeds the supported size.")
                            chunks.append(chunk)
                data = decode_object(b"".join(chunks))
                if data.get("error") is not None:
                    raise AIError("OpenRouter did not complete the model request.")
                choices = data.get("choices")
                if not isinstance(choices, list) or not choices or not isinstance(choices[0], dict):
                    raise ValueError("Invalid completion choices")
                choice = choices[0]
                if choice.get("finish_reason") != "stop":
                    raise AIError("Model response was incomplete. Use a smaller input or adjust the configured output limit.")
                message = choice.get("message")
                if not isinstance(message, dict):
                    raise ValueError("Invalid completion message")
                output = message.get("content")
                if not isinstance(output, str) or not output.strip():
                    raise AIError("OpenRouter returned no model output.")
                return output
            except httpx.TimeoutException:
                raise AIError("OpenRouter timed out; retry the request.", code="ai_timeout", status_code=504) from None
            except httpx.RequestError:
                raise AIError("Could not connect to OpenRouter.", code="ai_unavailable", status_code=503) from None
            except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, IndexError, RecursionError):
                raise AIError("OpenRouter returned an invalid response envelope.") from None

        def persist(self, request, prepared):
            """Persist validated preparation. Future AI extraction can use this boundary too."""
            if (request.organization_id, request.source_id) != (prepared.organization_id, prepared.source_id) or any(
                row.organization_id != request.organization_id for row in prepared.batch.records
            ):
                raise InputError("Prepared batch does not match the requested source/organization")
            replay_key = self._replay_key(request)
            try:
                with self.sessions.begin() as session:
                    # Serialize SQLite writers before identity reads, avoiding stale read-to-write upgrades.
                    session.connection(execution_options={"sqlite_write": True})
                    previous = session.scalar(select(IngestionRun).filter_by(**replay_key))
                    if previous is not None:
                        return previous.result | {"replayed": True}
                    return self._write(session, request, prepared, replay_key)
            except (IntegrityError, OperationalError) as exc:
                # A racing exact replay may have committed while this transaction lost a race.
                try:
                    with self.sessions() as session:
                        previous = session.scalar(select(IngestionRun).filter_by(**replay_key))
                        if previous is not None:
                            return previous.result | {"replayed": True}
                except OperationalError:
                    pass
                if isinstance(exc, OperationalError) and any(word in str(exc).lower() for word in ("locked", "busy")):
                    raise DatabaseBusy("Database is busy; retry the request") from exc
                raise
    
        def _write(self, session, request, prepared, replay_key):
            log = WarningLog(prepared)
            now = utc_now()
            run = IngestionRun(id=new_id(), **replay_key, format=request.format,
                               received_at=now, completed_at=now, result={})
            session.add(run)
            resolver = IdentityResolver(session, self.policy.aliases)
            records = prepared.batch.records
            roots = resolver.resolve_many([
                IdentityInput(f"r:{i}", row.ci_type, row.organization_id, row.identifiers)
                for i, row in enumerate(records)
            ])
            quarantined = 0
            for i, record in enumerate(records):
                resolved = roots[f"r:{i}"]
                if resolved.ci is None:
                    quarantined += 1
                    log.add("identity_conflict" if resolved.status == "identity_conflict" else "missing_identifiers",
                            record.record_key,
                            ("Conflicting identifiers: record retained without changing any CI" if resolved.status == "identity_conflict"
                             else "No trusted stable identifier: provide a source entity ID or configure a trusted identifier authority. Name-only records remain evidence."),
                            candidate_ids=list(resolved.candidate_ids))

    from starlette.requests import Request
    
    from app.api.errors import response
    from app.ingestion.parsing import MAX_BYTES
    
    
    class IngestBodyLimit:
        def __init__(self, app):
            self.app = app
    
        async def __call__(self, scope, receive, send):
            if scope["type"] != "http" or scope["method"] != "POST" or scope["path"] not in {"/ingest", "/ingest/raw"}:
                return await self.app(scope, receive, send)
            headers = dict(scope.get("headers", []))
            media = headers.get(b"content-type", b"").split(b";", 1)[0].lower()
            # JSON envelopes can escape each source character. The pipeline separately
            # checks decoded content against 1 MiB; multipart gets bounded form overhead.
            limit = 6 * MAX_BYTES + 65536 if media == b"application/json" else (
                MAX_BYTES + 65536 if media == b"multipart/form-data" else MAX_BYTES)
            chunks, size = [], 0
            while True:
                message = await receive()
                if message["type"] == "http.disconnect":
                    return
                chunk = message.get("body", b"")
                size += len(chunk)
                if size > limit:
                    result = response(Request(scope), 413, "limit_exceeded", "Upload exceeds the supported size (1 MiB of raw content).")
                    return await result(scope, receive, send)
                chunks.append(chunk)
                if not message.get("more_body", False):
                    break
            body = b"".join(chunks)
            delivered = False
            async def replay():
                nonlocal delivered
                if not delivered:
                    delivered = True
                    return {"type": "http.request", "body": body, "more_body": False}
                return await receive()
            await self.app(scope, replay, send)

        """Public API ingestion/read/ask flows, restarts and transaction recovery."""
        
        import json
        
        import pytest
        from sqlalchemy import func, select
        
        from app.db.models import ConfigurationItem, IngestionRun, Observation
        from .conftest import edge, eq, ingest, query_plan, snapshot
        
        
        def test_restart_cross_transport_replay_and_reformatted_duplicate(backend_factory):
            backend = backend_factory()
            rows = [{'device_id': 'D1', 'hostname': 'quoted "host"', 'status': 'active', 'os': 'macOS'}]
            content = json.dumps(rows)
            with backend.http() as client:
                first = ingest(client, rows)
                assert first.status_code == 200, first.text
                original = snapshot(backend)
                device_id = client.get('/devices').json()['data'][0]['id']
                detail = client.get('/ci/' + device_id).json()
                assert detail['provenance']['total'] == 1
                assert detail['provenance']['data'][0]['source_id'] == 'hardware'
                for result in [client.post('/ingest/raw?source_id=hardware', content=content, headers={'Content-Type': 'text/plain'}),
                               client.post('/ingest', json=dict(organization_id='org-a', source_id='hardware', format='json', content=content))]:
                    assert result.status_code == 200, result.text
                    assert result.json()['run_id'] == first.json()['run_id'] and result.json()['replayed'] is True
                assert snapshot(backend) == original
            backend.engine.dispose()
            restarted = backend_factory(name='integration')  # new engine, application and policy, same file
            with restarted.http() as client:
                replay = ingest(client, rows)
                assert replay.json()['replayed'] is True
                assert replay.json()['run_id'] == first.json()['run_id']
                assert client.get('/devices').json()['data'][0]['id'] == device_id
                assert snapshot(restarted) == original
                reformatted = client.post('/ingest/raw?source_id=hardware', content=json.dumps(rows, indent=2),
                                          headers={'Content-Type': 'text/plain'})
                assert reformatted.status_code == 200 and reformatted.json()['replayed'] is False
                assert client.get('/devices').json()['total'] == 1
                restarted.provider.planning(query_plan(where=[eq('status', 'active')], operation='count'))
                answer = client.post('/ask', json={'question': 'How many active devices are there?'}).json()
                assert answer['status'] == 'answered' and answer['total'] == 1 and answer['data'] is None
            assert not backend.provider.calls
            with restarted.sessions() as db:
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(IngestionRun)) == 2
                assert db.scalar(select(func.count()).select_from(Observation)) == 2
        
        
        def test_partial_identity_failure_commits_quarantine_without_corrupting_valid_entities(backend_factory):
            backend = backend_factory()
            with backend.http() as client:
                initial = ingest(client, [{'device_id': 'D1', 'serial_number': 'S1', 'hostname': 'one'},
                                          {'device_id': 'D2', 'serial_number': 'S2', 'hostname': 'two'}])
                assert initial.status_code == 200
                rows = [{'device_id': 'D1', 'serial_number': 'S2', 'hostname': 'wrong'},
                        {'hostname': 'keyless'}, {'device_id': 'D3', 'hostname': 'three'}]
                response = ingest(client, rows)
                assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
                body = response.json()
                assert body['records'] == dict(received=3, resolved=1, quarantined=2)
                assert {'identity_conflict', 'missing_identifiers'} <= {w['code'] for w in body['warnings']}
                assert {d['attributes']['hostname'] for d in client.get('/devices').json()['data']} == {'one', 'two', 'three'}
                backend.provider.planning(query_plan(operation='count'))

                original = snapshot(backend)

                assert len(conflicts) == 1 and conflicts[0].ci_id is None

        @pytest.mark.parametrize('stage', ['attributes', 'relationships', 'commit'])
        def test_http_failure_rolls_back_existing_changes_and_retries_cleanly(backend_factory, monkeypatch, stage):
            import app.ingestion.persistence as persistence
            from sqlalchemy import event
            backend = backend_factory()
            with backend.http() as client:
                assert ingest(client, [{'device_id': 'D1', 'hostname': 'original'}]).status_code == 200
                before = snapshot(backend)
                rows = [{'device_id': 'D1', 'hostname': 'changed'}, {'device_id': 'D2', 'hostname': 'new'}]
                def fail(*args):
                    raise RuntimeError('PRIVATE failure with SQL parameters and secret')
                with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
                    if stage == 'commit':
                        # Runs after all projections and flushes, immediately before commit.
                        event.listen(backend.engine, 'commit', fail)
                    else:
                        patch.setattr(persistence, 'project_attributes' if stage == 'attributes' else 'project_relationships', fail)
                    try:
                        result = ingest(client, rows)
                    finally:
                        if stage == 'commit':
                            event.remove(backend.engine, 'commit', fail)
                assert result.status_code == 500
                assert result.json()['error']['request_id'] == result.headers['x-request-id']
                assert 'PRIVATE' not in result.text and 'secret' not in result.text
                assert snapshot(backend) == before
                result = ingest(client, rows)
                assert result.status_code == 200 and result.json()['replayed'] is False
                devices = client.get('/devices').json()
                assert devices['total'] == 2
                old = next(d for d in devices['data'] if d['attributes']['hostname'] != 'new')
                assert old['attributes']['hostname'] is None and old['has_conflicts']  # both undated values retained
                assert ingest(client, rows).json()['replayed'] is True
        
        
        def test_real_sqlite_write_lock_has_uniform_error_then_recovers(backend_factory):
            backend = backend_factory()
            with backend.http() as client:
                assert ingest(client, [{'device_id': 'D1'}]).status_code == 200
                before = snapshot(backend)
                with backend.engine.connect().execution_options(sqlite_write=True) as connection:
                    with connection.begin():
                        result = ingest(client, [{'device_id': 'D2'}])
                        assert result.status_code == 503
                        assert result.json()['error']['code'] == 'database_busy'
                        assert result.json()['error']['request_id'] == result.headers['x-request-id']
                assert snapshot(backend) == before
                assert ingest(client, [{'device_id': 'D2'}]).status_code == 200
                assert client.get('/devices').json()['total'] == 2

        from copy import deepcopy
        import json
        
        import httpx
        import pytest

        def synthetic_export():
            rows = [
                dict(id='D-42', kind='device', attrs=dict(hostname='build-laptop', os_family='macos', status='active'),
                     links=[('assigned_to', 1)]),
                dict(id='U-42', kind='user', attrs=dict(name='Morgan', mfa_enabled=False), links=[('uses', 2)]),
                dict(id='A-42', kind='application', attrs=dict(name='Toolbox'),
                     links=[('depends_on', 3), ('integrates_with', 3), ('owned_by', 1)]),
                dict(id='A-43', kind='application', attrs=dict(name='DataHub'), links=[]),
            ]
            def pointer(path):
                return dict(pointer=path)
            def identifier(index):
                kind = rows[index]['kind']
                return dict(identifier_type={'device': 'device_id', 'user': 'user_id', 'application': 'app_id'}[kind],
                            value=rows[index]['id'], evidence=pointer(f'/export_rows/{index}/id'))
            records = []
            for index, row in enumerate(rows):
                path = f'/export_rows/{index}'
                records.append(dict(ci_type=row['kind'], attributes=row['attrs'],
                    attribute_evidence={k: pointer(path + '/attrs/' + k) for k in row['attrs']},
                    identifiers=[identifier(index)], evidence=pointer(path), relationships=[
                        dict(relation_type=relation, evidence=pointer(f'{path}/links/{j}'),
                             target=dict(ci_type=rows[target]['kind'], identifiers=[identifier(target)],
                                         evidence=pointer(f'/export_rows/{target}')))
                        for j, (relation, target) in enumerate(row['links'])]))
            return json.dumps(dict(export_rows=rows)), dict(records=records)
        
        
        def test_upload_extraction_preview_ask_provenance_and_restart_replay(backend_factory):
            backend = backend_factory()
            content, extracted = synthetic_export()
            backend.provider.outputs['cmdb_extraction'] = extracted
            p = query_plan(exists=[edge('assigned_to', 'user', [eq('mfa_enabled', False)],
                                       [edge('uses', 'application', [eq('name', 'Toolbox')])])])
            backend.provider.planning(p)
            question = 'Which devices belong to users without MFA who use Toolbox?'
            with backend.http() as client:
                uploaded = client.post('/ingest', files={'file': ('custom.json', content, 'application/json')}, data={'source_id': 'notes'})
                assert uploaded.status_code == 200, uploaded.text
                assert uploaded.json()['entities']['created'] == 4
                assert uploaded.json()['relationships']['created'] == 5
                device = client.get('/devices').json()['data'][0]
                device_id = device['id']
                detail = client.get('/ci/' + device_id).json()
                assert detail['provenance']['data'][0]['origin'] == 'ai'
                assert detail['field_state']['hostname']['evidence'][0]['extraction_evidence']['pointer'].endswith('/attrs/hostname')
                before = snapshot(backend)
                preview = client.post('/ask/plan', json={'question': question})
                assert preview.status_code == 200 and preview.json()['executed'] is False
                answer = client.post('/ask', json={'question': question, 'limit': 1})
                assert answer.status_code == 200, answer.text
                assert answer.json()['total'] == 1 and answer.json()['data'][0]['id'] == device_id
                assert answer.json()['resolved_references'][0]['ci_id']
                assert snapshot(backend) == before  # preview and answer are read-only
                for relation in ['depends_on', 'integrates_with']:
                    backend.provider.planning(query_plan('application', exists=[edge(relation, 'application', [eq('name', 'DataHub')])]))
                    result = client.post('/ask', json={'question': f'Which applications {relation} DataHub?'}).json()
                    assert result['total'] == 1 and result['data'][0]['attributes']['name'] == 'Toolbox'
                backend.provider.planning(query_plan('application', exists=[edge('owned_by', 'user', [eq('name', 'Morgan')])]))
                assert client.post('/ask', json={'question': 'Which applications are owned by Morgan?'}).json()['total'] == 1
            backend.engine.dispose()
            restarted = backend_factory(provider=backend.provider)
            calls_before = len(backend.provider.calls)
            with restarted.http() as client:
                replay = client.post('/ingest/raw?source_id=notes', content=content, headers={'Content-Type': 'text/plain'})
                assert replay.status_code == 200 and replay.json()['replayed'] is True
                assert replay.json()['run_id'] == uploaded.json()['run_id']
                assert len(backend.provider.calls) == calls_before
                assert snapshot(restarted) == before
            # Only interpretation metadata/question reach the planner, never DB records.
            for call in backend.provider.calls:
                if call['response_format']['json_schema']['name'] == 'cmdb_query_plan':
                    text = json.dumps(call)
                    assert device_id not in text and 'build-laptop' not in text
        
        
        @pytest.mark.parametrize('route', ['extract', 'ask'])
        @pytest.mark.parametrize('fault,status,expected_calls', [
            ('timeout', 504, 1), ('rate_limit', 503, 1), ('provider_error', 503, 1),
            ('invalid_envelope', 502, 1), ('invalid_json', 502, 2), ('unsafe_output', 502, 2),
        ])
        def test_provider_failures_preserve_existing_database_and_recover(backend_factory, route, fault, status, expected_calls):
            backend = backend_factory()
            content, good = synthetic_export()
            with backend.http() as client:
                assert ingest(client, [{'device_id': 'existing', 'status': 'active'}]).status_code == 200
                before = snapshot(backend)
                if fault == 'timeout':
                    bad = httpx.ReadTimeout('PRIVATE upstream detail')
                elif fault in {'rate_limit', 'provider_error'}:
                    bad = httpx.Response(429 if fault == 'rate_limit' else 500, text='PRIVATE provider body')
                elif fault == 'invalid_envelope':
                    bad = httpx.Response(200, json={'choices': None, 'private': 'PRIVATE provider body'})
                elif fault == 'invalid_json':
                    bad = 'PRIVATE not JSON'
                elif route == 'extract':
                    bad = deepcopy(good)
                    bad['records'][0]['identifiers'][0]['value'] = 'INVENTED-ID'
                else:
                    bad = dict(result=dict(status='planned', plan=dict(root='device', operation='delete', sql='DROP TABLE devices')))
                schema = 'cmdb_extraction' if route == 'extract' else 'cmdb_query_plan'
                backend.provider.outputs[schema] = bad
                def submit():
                    if route == 'extract':
                        return client.post('/ingest/raw?source_id=notes', content=content, headers={'Content-Type': 'text/plain'})
                    return client.post('/ask', json={'question': 'How many active devices are there?'})
                response = submit()
                assert response.status_code == status, response.text
                assert response.json()['error']['request_id'] == response.headers['x-request-id']
                assert 'PRIVATE' not in response.text and 'integration-test-key' not in response.text
                assert len(backend.provider.calls) == expected_calls
                assert snapshot(backend) == before
                if route == 'extract':
                    backend.provider.outputs[schema] = good
                    recovered = submit()
                    assert recovered.status_code == 200 and recovered.json()['replayed'] is False
                else:
                    backend.provider.planning(query_plan(where=[eq('status', 'active')], operation='count'))
                    recovered = submit()
                    assert recovered.status_code == 200 and recovered.json()['total'] == 1
                    assert snapshot(backend) == before
        EOF

        """Supplied fixtures are test cases, not identity or conflict policy in code."""
        
        import json
        from pathlib import Path
        
        import pytest
        from sqlalchemy import select
        
        from app.api.inventory_service import InventoryService
        from app.db.models import ConfigurationItem, Relationship
        from app.reconciliation.policy import load_sources
        from .conftest import edge, eq, query_plan, snapshot
        
        ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
        MANIFEST = json.loads((ROOT / 'examples/sample_sources.json').read_text())
        
        
        def upload_all(client, order):
            for index, file_index in enumerate(order):
                entry = MANIFEST[file_index]
                source = entry['source']
                content = (ROOT / 'input_data' / entry['file']).read_text()
                fmt = 'yaml' if source['adapter'] == 'hardware_yaml' else 'csv' if source['adapter'] == 'hardware_csv' else 'json'
                if index % 3 == 0:
                    result = client.post('/ingest', files={'file': (entry['file'], content)}, data={'source_id': source['source_id']})
                elif index % 3 == 1:
                    result = client.post('/ingest/raw', params={'source_id': source['source_id']}, content=content,
                                         headers={'Content-Type': 'text/plain'})
                else:
                    result = client.post('/ingest', json=dict(organization_id=source['organization_id'],
                        source_id=source['source_id'], format=fmt, content=content))
                assert result.status_code == 200, result.text
                yield result.json()
        
        
        def semantic_snapshot(backend):
            """Compare projections/edges by stable identifiers, ignoring generated UUIDs."""
            with backend.sessions() as db:
                items = list(db.scalars(select(ConfigurationItem)))
                keys = {ci.id: tuple(sorted((key.namespace, key.value) for key in ci.identifiers)) for ci in items}
                inventory = InventoryService(db, 'example-corp')
                records = [dict(key=keys[ci.id], kind=ci.kind, display_name=ci.display_name, reference=ci.is_reference,
                                attributes=inventory.view(ci)['attributes'],
                                states={field: state['status'] for field, state in ci.field_state.items()}) for ci in items]
                edges = [(keys[edge.from_ci_id], edge.relation_type, keys[edge.to_ci_id])
                         for edge in db.scalars(select(Relationship))]
            return sorted(json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True) for r in records), sorted(edges)
        
        
        @pytest.mark.parametrize('order', [(4, 3, 2, 1, 0), (3, 4, 0, 2, 1), (2, 0, 4, 1, 3)])
        def test_fixture_orders_transports_replay_and_grounded_answers(backend_factory, order):
            sources = load_sources(ROOT / 'examples/sample_sources.json')
            baseline = backend_factory(sources=sources, name='baseline')
            with baseline.http() as client:
                list(upload_all(client, range(5)))
            backend = backend_factory(sources=sources, name='permuted')
            with backend.http() as client:
                summaries = list(upload_all(client, order))
                assert not any(s['replayed'] for s in summaries)
                assert semantic_snapshot(backend) == semantic_snapshot(baseline)
                assert [client.get(path).json()['total'] for path in ['/devices', '/users', '/apps']] == [3, 12, 28]
                before = snapshot(backend)
                replayed = list(upload_all(client, tuple(reversed(order))))
                assert all(s['replayed'] for s in replayed)
                assert {s['run_id'] for s in replayed} == {s['run_id'] for s in summaries}
                assert snapshot(backend) == before

    # Backend Take-Home Assignment
    
    ## Build an AI-First Configuration Management Database (CMDB)
    
    **Recommended timebox:** 6-8 hours
    **Focus:** Data modeling, AI integration, backend systems thinking
    **Language:** Python
    **AI usage:** Strongly encouraged with session transcripts
    
    ---
    
    ## What we are looking for
    
    We care most about your ability to model complex, interconnected data and apply AI thoughtfully to real problems. A well-reasoned data model with clear tradeoffs is better than a broad feature set with shallow coverage. We evaluate the `/ingest` and `/ask` endpoints most heavily.
    
    We look holistically at: code quality and structure, AI integration and reasoning, data modeling and storage choices, API design, and documentation. There are no fixed weights — strong work in any area can stand out.
    
    While we do not expect a production-ready system in the submission, your design would need to be the foundation of one. Thinking about how to scale, what to optimize, metrics to observe, and design tradeoffs for such a system would be the key discussion points on your submission.
    
    ## Context
    
    You are building a runnable prototype of an AI-powered Configuration Management Database (CMDB) backend service. The system ingests raw or semi-structured IT infrastructure data, extracts and normalizes configuration items (CIs), stores them in a database, and uses AI to assist when necessary.
    
    # Core Scope (required)
    
    ## Objective
    
    Your solution should:
    
    1. Ingest raw or semi-structured data from IT infrastructure and/or third-party SaaS applications.
    2. Extract and normalize configuration items (CIs).
    3. Store the structured data in any database of your choice.
    4. Use AI to assist with one or more of the following:
       - Parsing and structuring input data.
       - Enriching missing or inconsistent fields.
       - Responding to natural language queries.
    
    ## Input Data Sources
    
    We've provided some sample input data, but feel free to find/generate more of your own if you wish. The data could be any of the following:
    
    ### Physical Infrastructure Examples
    
    - JSON exports from Jamf, SCCM, or GLPI.
    - CSV or YAML files representing hardware inventory.
    - SNMP/NetBox-style records (e.g., hostname, MAC address, physical location).
    - Simulated or manually generated hardware data.
    
    ### SaaS Application Examples
    
    - Okta user and app assignment exports.
    - GitHub organization metadata.
    - Atlassian/Jira project exports.
    - Salesforce or Workday usage reports.
    - Slack workspace configuration data.
    
    ## Configuration Items (CIs) to Extract
    
    From the input data, extract and normalize the following:
    
    ### Device
    
    - Hostname, IP address, OS, assigned user, location, status.
    
    ### User
    
    - Name, team, assigned applications, MFA status, last login.
    
    ### App
    
    - Name, owner, type (SaaS/on-prem), integrations, usage count.
    
    ### Relationships
    
    - Device ownership.
    - App usage.
    - Dependencies between different Apps/Devices
    
    ## Storage
    
    Use any database of your choice. Clearly justify your data model and technology choice in the README. Some options include:
    
    - SQL: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite.
    - Graph DB: Neo4j, etc.
    - NoSQL: MongoDB, DynamoDB.
    - Embedded: TinyDB, Redis.
    
    ## API Requirements
    
    Build a REST API using Python that includes:
    
    - `POST /ingest`: Upload raw input data.
    - `GET /devices`, `GET /users`, `GET /apps`: List CIs.
    - `GET /ci/<id>`: Fetch details by ID.
    - `POST /ask`: Handle natural language queries (e.g., "Which users don't have MFA?").
    
    ## AI Usage
    
    You may use OpenAI, HuggingFace, LangChain, or similar tools. You may also mock AI responses where needed — just be sure to explain your approach.
    
    ---
    
    # Implementation Guidelines
    
    ## What to prioritize
    
    - A clear, well-justified data model for CIs and their relationships
    - Thoughtful AI integration that adds real value
    - Clean API design with good separation of concerns
    - Reasoning about tradeoffs in your README
    
    ## What we do not expect
    
    - Perfect coverage of every edge case — pick a coherent slice and document choices
